findings.title: The new NO_NEW_SCAN copies end 'and these pages can go through then', and the round-6 composition strips the outcome's own requirement (JPEG/PNG, split the worksheet, a clearer photo) before appending that promise
findings.claim_under_review: ARCHIVED_CHILD_NO_NEW_SCAN_COPY / INACTIVE_CHILD_NO_NEW_SCAN_COPY: "… Activate the profile again on the Children page, while a paid slot is free, and these pages can go through then." / "… Assign one of your family’s unused paid slots to this profile on the Children page, while one is free, and these pages can go through then."
findings.mechanism: apps/web/src/pages/app/HomeworkPage.tsx:246-252, path 1 of `explainStatus`: when `noNewScanCopy(childStatus)` is non-null and the row has a permanent code, the page prints `OUTCOME_WITHOUT_NEW_SCAN_ADVICE[code]` followed by the blocker constant. That table (HomeworkPage.tsx:183-196) deliberately holds the code's sentence WITH its remedy removed: FORMAT_NEEDS_CONVERSION loses 'Scan the pages again as JPEG or PNG photos.' (the full line is at HomeworkPage.tsx:146-147), SCAN_TOO_MANY_QUESTIONS loses 'Split it into two scans with fewer pages each.' (148-149), and path 3 (HomeworkPage.tsx:262-266) does the same for `needs_rescan`, dropping 'ask <name> to scan again with a clearer picture' from STATUS_COPY (HomeworkPage.tsx:112-116). The appended constant then asserts that once the profile is fixed 'these pages can go through then'. They cannot: a PDF/HEIC file is still unreadable (`HomeworkMimeType` rejects it at POST /v1/assignments), a worksheet with more questions than one check handles still exceeds the stage limit, and the same blurred photos are still unreadable. The removal is actively pinned: apps/web/src/pages/app/HomeworkPage.test.tsx:1354-1382 asserts /PDF or HEIC/ present and /Scan the pages again as JPEG or PNG/ present only for an ACTIVE child (1401-1411).
findings.impact: A parent whose child was demoted by a store downgrade, or archived, reads on the Homework page: the file format could not be read / the worksheet had too many questions, then 'Assign one of your family’s unused paid slots … and these pages can go through then.' They assign or buy a slot on the strength of that sentence, re-send the same PDF or the same oversized worksheet, and it fails again for the reason the page has just stopped telling them. On the slot-purchase path that is a paid action taken on a false promise.
findings.ruled_out: I checked that `explainStatus` returns exactly one string, so no other sentence on the row or in the detail panel restores the requirement (HomeworkPage.tsx:239-268). I checked `statusLabel` (HomeworkPage.tsx:203-206) only relabels and adds no advice. I checked that path 1 returns before path 2, so FAILED_FINAL_COPY's complete line (which does carry the requirement) is unreachable for these codes when the profile is non-active. I checked the blocker half of the constants is TRUE — readPaidProfile's `entitled` requires `status = 'active'` (apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:410-414) and assertCanCollect refuses create, upload and finalize (homework.ts:421-451) — so the defect is the closing promise, not the blocker. I checked CONSENT_REQUIRED is deliberately kept WHOLE by path 2 precisely so its own remedy survives (HomeworkPage.tsx:253-258), which shows the trimming for these three outcomes was a choice rather than an oversight.
findings.reproduction: apps/web/src/pages/app/HomeworkPage.test.tsx, in the '[HUNT6-H-2]' describe: for ARCHIVED_FAMILY / DRAFT_FAMILY with a `failed_final` row whose errorCode is FORMAT_NEEDS_CONVERSION, assert the row still tells the parent the pages must be JPEG or PNG (and, for SCAN_TOO_MANY_QUESTIONS, that the worksheet must be split). Red today, because line 1409's assertion is the negation of it.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep each code's own requirement in OUTCOME_WITHOUT_NEW_SCAN_ADVICE — trim only the imperative 'scan again', not the condition ('…so this scan was not checked and its pages were given back; PencilLift needs JPEG or PNG photos.' / '…split into two scans with fewer pages each.') — and end the two contract constants with the profile step alone, without asserting that these pages will then go through (e.g. '… and new scans can go through then.').

findings.title: 'Here rather than in a page so the portal and the app say the same thing' is false for the two new constants: the app never imports them, and its child result view still tells a slotless child to scan again — the one non-active state that does NOT revoke the child's session
findings.claim_under_review: "Both name the Children page … Here rather than in a page so the portal and the app say the same thing, beside the two lines they replace the advice of."
findings.mechanism: ARCHIVED_CHILD_NO_NEW_SCAN_COPY and INACTIVE_CHILD_NO_NEW_SCAN_COPY are imported by exactly one file, apps/web/src/pages/app/HomeworkPage.tsx:30-34; nothing under apps/mobile imports either, and the app has no parent-facing assignment list at all (apps/mobile/src/homework/ holds child-api.ts, upload.ts, result-view.ts — the child's screens; the only '/v1/assignments' calls in apps/mobile are the child's upload path, upload.ts:204-290). The app DOES have a surface that gives the advice the round-6 constants exist to remove: apps/mobile/src/homework/result-view.ts:131-137, `statusView('needs_rescan')` returns 'Some pages were hard to read. Try scanning them again in good light, flat on a table.' for every profile status, and result-view.ts:148-156 (`failed_final`) offers 'try a new scan'. That is reachable for the `draft` case, because a downgrade-driven demotion revokes nothing: apps/api/src/services/billing-sync.ts:1314-1332 (`releaseSlotlessProfiles`) only sets `status = 'draft'`, unlike apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:537 (archive) and public.request_deletion, which both revoke `child_sessions`. So the demoted child's paired tablet still renders the rescan advice, and POST /v1/assignments then refuses with CHILD_NOT_ACTIVE (apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:439-451).
findings.impact: A child whose family's plan lapsed opens their results, is told to photograph the worksheet again in good light, does it, and is stopped at send with 'Ask a grown-up to help with scanning right now.' The wasted effort falls on a 5-13-year-old, and the round-6 comment asserts this surface is covered, so a later reader will not look for it. The claim is the same over-claim the round-6 change to packages/contracts/src/account.ts:75-80 (HUNT6-F-SHARED-COPY) went out of its way to correct two files away.
findings.ruled_out: I checked whether mobile has any parent homework surface that the constants could serve (it does not: the parent surfaces are apps/mobile/src/privacy, family, billing, learning, rewards, support). I checked whether an ARCHIVED child could reach the app's result view — it cannot, family.ts:537 and public.request_deletion both revoke `child_sessions` — so the reachable case is precisely the `draft`/downgrade one, which is also the commoner population the constant's own G-DRAFT comment identifies. I checked that the child's refusal message is itself age-appropriate and not a leak (homework.ts:443-449 passes a child-facing string), so the defect is the advice printed BEFORE it plus the false shared-copy claim, not the refusal. I checked the two sibling constants (ARCHIVED_CHILD_SCAN_COPY, INACTIVE_CHILD_SCAN_COPY) and CONSENT_WITHDRAWN_SCAN_COPY carry the same sentence, so the phrase is house style — which is why the claim needs deciding rather than repeating.
findings.reproduction: apps/mobile/src/homework/result-view.test.ts:99 currently asserts `statusView('needs_rescan').title` and body unconditionally; a new case that asks for the `needs_rescan` view of a child whose profile has no paid slot and asserts the body does not tell the child to scan again is red today (the function takes only `AssignmentStatus`, so it cannot even express the case).
findings.suggested_fix: Decide the claim: either delete the 'so the portal and the app say the same thing' sentence from the two new constants (and say plainly that the app has no parent homework surface today), or give the app the same distinction — pass the child's profile state into `statusView` and, for a child with no paid slot, replace 'Try scanning them again' with a calm child-facing line that names no billing ('New scans are paused right now. Ask a grown-up.'), which is what assertCanCollect already says at the refusal.

findings.title: Every 'still bounded' assertion the round-6 widening touched is satisfied by ~200 rows against a 400 bound, so the system and child kinds' second windows can lose their LIMIT with no test going red
findings.claim_under_review: "Still bounded: at most two pages of that kind, never the whole open queue (CS-R4-01)" (line 1052) and "the whole open queue is still never returned — 206 open child reports are all listed here because 206 is under that bound, not because the branch is unbounded" (lines 927-931)
findings.mechanism: Four assertions assert `<= 2 * UNRESOLVED_REPORTS_PAGE_SIZE` (400) against data sets that never approach it: line 937 with 206 open child reports (1 + UNRESOLVED_REPORTS_PAGE_SIZE + 5, lines 909-921), line 1053 with 202 open system flags (UNRESOLVED_REPORTS_PAGE_SIZE filler + the real flag + one more, lines 1022-1040), line 1095 with 203 child reports (lines 1064-1078) and line 1134 with 201 parent reports (lines 1109-1117). The round-6 diff changed line 937 from `<= UNRESOLVED_REPORTS_PAGE_SIZE + 1` (201, which DID bite at 206 rows) to `<= 400`, which cannot. The only cases that reach the bound — line 634 and line 720, `toHaveLength(2 * UNRESOLVED_REPORTS_PAGE_SIZE)` over 405 rows — exercise the PARENT kind alone. So deleting `limit ${UNRESOLVED_REPORTS_PAGE_SIZE}` from `newest_flags` (apps/api/src/routes/privacy.ts:948-950) or from `newest_child` (privacy.ts:966-968) leaves the whole suite green, although privacy.ts:167-171 states the two-page bound as the response's guarantee. Separately, the HUNT5-B-5 docstring (lines 950-958) and its inline comment (line 982) still describe the removed one-row window as current: "the NEWEST unresolved row of each kind is always in the response as well" / "the drain window plus at most the newest row of that kind".
findings.impact: The response bound on the two kinds that matter most — system flags and a child's own reports — is unpinned. A later change that drops or widens either second window (the exact edit round 6 made in the other direction) ships green, and a family with a long flag queue gets an unbounded /v1/safety-reports response on the surface the flag email names. Nobody is harmed today; the guarantee simply is not tested.
findings.ruled_out: I checked that the parent kind IS pinned: lines 634 and 720 use 405 rows with an exact `toHaveLength(400)`, so those bite. I checked that line 986's exact `toHaveLength(UNRESOLVED_REPORTS_PAGE_SIZE + 1)` does not pin the limit either — with 201 open flags only one row remains outside the drain window, so the count is 201 with or without the LIMIT on newest_flags. I grepped for UNRESOLVED_REPORTS_PAGE_SIZE across the repo and found no other test that exercises more than 400 reports of one kind. I checked the bound itself is correctly implemented (oldest-200 ∪ newest-200-of-the-remainder is exactly both ends), so this is a test gap, not a behaviour defect.
findings.reproduction: apps/api/tests/privacy-r2.review.test.ts — one case inserting 2 * UNRESOLVED_REPORTS_PAGE_SIZE + 5 open `system` flags and asserting `toHaveLength(2 * UNRESOLVED_REPORTS_PAGE_SIZE)`, plus its `child` twin. The mutation that proves they bite: remove `limit ${UNRESOLVED_REPORTS_PAGE_SIZE}` from `newest_flags` in apps/api/src/routes/privacy.ts:950.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the two exact-count cases above (system and child, 405 rows each, `toHaveLength(400)` on that kind's unresolved rows) beside the existing parent-kind cases, and rewrite the HUNT5-B-5 docstring and its line-982 comment to describe the page-sized second window instead of the one-row one it replaced.

findings.title: The bound's 'for every kind, with no exception' is quantified over reporter kinds, but the third window pair covers a SET of kinds — and the contract enum means a kind added later is not 'listed' but breaks the whole list
findings.claim_under_review: "what can be absent is stated exactly: rows in the MIDDLE of a kind's queue, once that kind has more than 400 unresolved rows open at once — never the oldest of a kind and never its newest, for every kind, with no exception" (privacy.ts:167-171), resting on "The catch-all branch (today: 'parent', the only other kind migration 0760 permits), so a reporter kind added later is listed rather than silently dropped from the family's list" (privacy.ts:969-971)
findings.mechanism: `unresolved_parent` and the new `oldest_parent` (privacy.ts:972-987) both select `reporter_kind not in ('system', 'child')`, so their two pages hold the oldest and newest of that SET, not of each kind in it. The comment beside them justifies the branch as future-proofing for an added kind; the moment a second kind lives in the set, the quantified claim above is false for it — its oldest and newest rows can both be absent once the combined set exceeds 400 open rows — and nothing says so. The same future-proofing claim is false for a second reason: `safetyReportReporterKindSchema` is a closed `z.enum(['child','parent','system'])` (packages/contracts/src/privacy.ts:186) and both clients call `safetyReportsResponseSchema.parse` (apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.tsx, apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.ts:363-380), so a row with a new kind does not get 'listed' — it throws and the family's whole safety list fails to render.
findings.impact: Nothing today. It is the shape that keeps costing rounds here: a quantified invariant with one case silently excused, and a stated reason for a new CTE that the contract contradicts. A later migration that widens `safety_reports_reporter_kind_check` would take out the family's entire report list rather than list the new kind, and would quietly break the absence guarantee the comment says holds with no exception.
findings.ruled_out: I checked reachability before filing: `reporter_kind` is NOT NULL and constrained to ('child','parent','system') (supabase/migrations/0600_operations.sql:181, widened once by 0760_safety_screening.sql:24-26), so no row today falls outside all three branches and no NULL can slip past `not in`. I checked the union cannot duplicate a row — each second window carries `id not in (select id from <first window>)` and `id` is non-null, so NOT IN is safe and the disjointness half of the claim holds. I checked the three window pairs are genuinely per-kind for the two real kinds, so the claim is true of the tree as shipped; the defect is the scope of the words, not the behaviour.
findings.reproduction: No production reproduction exists (the check constraint forbids it). The honest test is a documentation-level one in supabase/tests/hardening_r2_db.test.ts style: assert that `safety_reports_reporter_kind_check` still permits exactly the three kinds the contract enum lists, so widening one without the other is red.
findings.suggested_fix: Narrow the wording at privacy.ts:167-171 to the kinds the schema permits ('for each of the three reporter kinds migration 0760 permits'), and replace the 'a reporter kind added later is listed' rationale at privacy.ts:969-971 with what is true — the branch keeps an unexpected kind out of the flag and child windows, and adding a kind requires widening safetyReportReporterKindSchema and giving that kind its own window pair.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: Migration 0920's headline property: a deletion withdraws every finished export file that holds the deleted data as soon as it is requested, on EVERY surface including the Data API.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Traced the Data-API path (public.request_deletion granted to `authenticated`, 0920:148-149) against apps/api/src/routes/export-download.ts, which reads only kind/status/storage_path/expires_at. Then attacked the one row class the migration deliberately leaves alone: a 'queued' export. Under READ COMMITTED, `childrenBeingDeleted` (apps/api/src/jobs/export-build.ts:556-564) is the FIRST statement of the build transaction, so a deletion committing after it and before the data selects yields a family_data file containing the deleted child's homework, transcriptions and results — and the final write, `update … set status='ready' … where status='queued'` (export-build.ts:728-733), still matches because neither 0920 nor withdrawExports touches 'queued'. Then I checked whether that file or row could outlive the purge.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: app.purge_family_data's export_ids includes `child_id is null` rows for a CHILD purge (supabase/migrations/0820_support_cases_purge.sql:49-51), so the family-wide row is deleted and the build's final UPDATE matches nothing; the same list deletes the export_build job itself (0820:56-66), so an unstarted build never runs. runDeletionPurge (apps/api/src/jobs/dispatcher.ts:283-317) removes the three deterministic paths of every 'queued' export AND schedules a second removal at now + LATE_UPLOAD_WINDOW_MS (3 hours, dispatcher.ts:123), so bytes uploaded after the purge are still taken out, with no row left to download them through. The race therefore cannot leave a downloadable file.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: The API's withdraw predicate and migration 0920's agree: neither withdraws less than the other, and neither expires an export that does not hold the deleted data.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Compared apps/api/src/routes/privacy.ts:383-397 with 0920/0930's `update public.data_exports` statement column by column, then looked for an export kind that carries child X's rows under a different child_id (which the scope predicate would miss), and for an 'expired' row whose expires_at could still be in the future (which would make the migration's 'changes no column' claim false).
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: Both use `(p_child is null or child_id = p_child or child_id is null)`, so the scope is identical; the handler's extra arm (`status='expired' and storage_path is not null`) is strictly wider and exists only to feed `returning storage_path` into the object removal, exactly as documented. No export kind carries one child's rows under another child's id (export-build.ts builds child-scoped kinds from `row.child_id` and family-wide kinds from the family with a skip list). Every path that sets 'expired' also pulls expires_at back to `least(…, now())`, so an already-expired row cannot hold a future expiry and the migration's narrower arm really does change nothing.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: CS-R4-01's property, kept through the round-6 widening: a parent's own reports can never consume the room a system flag needs, and below 400 open rows of a kind neither that kind's oldest nor its newest unresolved row is absent.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Reconstructed all six CTEs (privacy.ts:938-995) and checked (a) that the two windows of a kind can overlap or leave a gap, (b) the tie case — two flags from one scan share `created_at`, because scan-process.ts:2306-2317 inserts them in one transaction where now() is the transaction timestamp — and (c) `id not in (select id from <cte>)` when the first window is empty or when ids could be NULL.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: oldest-200 ∪ newest-200-of-the-remainder is exactly both ends of a kind, with only the middle absent above 400, which is what the comment states. Per-kind windows mean the catch-all branch cannot displace a flag whatever its size. `id` is the primary key, so NOT IN never evaluates to NULL, and an empty first window makes it trivially true. Ties only make the arbitrary choice inside a window arbitrary, never push a row out of both windows below the bound.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: Child privacy on the two round-6 surfaces: GET /v1/safety-reports cannot tell the family WHICH kind of concern was flagged, and the family_data export cannot carry a safety notice's wording.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Checked REPORT_COLUMNS (privacy.ts:216-217) against the only SELECT grant `authenticated` holds (0760_safety_screening.sql:172-181) and the policy's full history (0600:302, 0670:13-14, 0760:185-187, with no later redefinition). Then tried to defeat the round-6 HUNT6-B-5 key check by imagining a new column added to export-build's childFeedback select, and checked whether a null-valued or reordered column could slip past it.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: screen_categories, screen_version, resolution_note and family_visible are not granted and not selected, and the final policy is `app.is_family_member(family_id) and family_visible`, so a held report is invisible through both the handler and RLS. The replacement assertion (privacy-r2.review.test.ts:826-830) takes `Object.keys` of a row parsed out of the REAL export JSON and compares with order-sensitive `toEqual`, and JSON.stringify keeps null-valued keys, so any column added anywhere in export-build.ts:517-526's select — including a null one — changes the array and reds the case. It is no longer a tautology.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: HUNT6-B-4's property: a lock-contention SQLSTATE from the belt-and-braces slot release still reaches app.ts as a retryable 503, while everything else stays hidden from POST /deletion's 42501 / 23505 / P0002 branches.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Enumerated every throw site inside releaseChildSlot (privacy.ts:566-576): both `set local role` statements and the UPDATE. Checked whether any of 40P01/40001/55P03 could collide with a branch in the handler's catch (privacy.ts:675-697), whether a 42501 from a lost grant could now escape unwrapped, and whether a transient error could leave the deletion request committed.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: isTransientDbError matches only 40P01, 40001 and 55P03 (apps/api/src/errors.ts:102-105), and the handler branches on 23505, P0002 and 42501 — disjoint sets, so a passed-through transient code reaches app.ts unclaimed. A 42501 is not transient, so it is still wrapped in SlotReleaseFailed and cannot be reported as a missing PIN. Any error inside the callback aborts and rolls back the postgres.js transaction, so nothing lands; the paired test cases (privacy-r2.review.test.ts:1152-1226 and 1228-1290) assert both the 503 and that no deletion request survives.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: POST /deletion cannot act on the wrong family, although callerMembership does not fail closed the way currentFamilyId does.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: callerMembership (privacy.ts:325-336) takes `const [row]` from a query with no ORDER BY and no LIMIT, while currentFamilyId (apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts:102-119) reads two rows and throws CONFLICT on a second — so I looked for any way for one adult to hold two active memberships, which would let an irreversible family deletion pick a family arbitrarily while every other route refused.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: supabase/migrations/0720_identity_hardening.sql:18-19 creates `family_memberships_one_active_family_per_user`, a unique index on (user_id) WHERE status = 'active'. Two active memberships cannot exist, so the arbitrary pick has at most one candidate and public.request_deletion re-checks membership and ownership for whichever family is passed.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: HUNT6-B-6's premise, which family.ts's deletion-pending listing rationale rests on: no surface cancels a deletion request.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Read the widened scan (family-hardening-r4.review.test.ts:355-404) and tried to get past it: a status written from a variable rather than the literal 'cancelled', a route registered outside apps/api/src/routes (e.g. in app.ts), a router mounted under a '/deletion' prefix so its own paths do not contain the word, and a double-quoted or backtick path literal. Then I checked the underlying fact independently.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: Every write of deletion_requests.status in the tree sets 'completed' with completed_at (0620:232-235, 0710:520-523, 0820:144-147), and 'processing' is never written at all; grep confirms the only HTTP registrations naming deletion are GET /deletion and POST /deletion. The scan's residual holes (app.ts, a variable-valued status) are real but do not make the claim false today, so family.ts's rationale is sound and I did not file it.

findings.title: A refused sign-out cannot clear the session auth-js holds when localStorage is unusable, and the callers' re-read reports that session as gone — so the portal says "This computer is signed out" over a session that comes back when the network does
findings.claim_under_review: "Storage blocked (site data blocked, a locked-down browser): merely touching localStorage throws, so auth-js's supportsLocalStorage() is false and this origin's session is held in its memoryLocalStorageAdapter instead — where a localStorage removal cannot reach it. Nothing is removed here, and nothing was persisted either, so that session cannot outlive the tab; what this function can establish is unchanged, which is why the report stays about the server alone and the callers read the session for themselves (HUNT6-F-3, HUNT6-F-PREMISE)." (supabase-auth.ts:184-189)
findings.mechanism:
Round 6's remedy for BUG-322/BUG-323 is: the adapter stops claiming this origin's session is gone, and every caller that would say so re-reads `currentSession()` (apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:80-82, :116-119; apps/web/src/components/SignOutControl.tsx:70-77; apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:744-750). The read cannot establish that fact, and on the one refusal path that matters it returns the wrong answer.

(1) When localStorage is unusable, auth-js does not keep the session in localStorage at all. GoTrueClient.js:249-269: with `persistSession: true` and no `storage` option (apps/web/src/lib/supabase-auth.ts:131-141 passes none), `this.storage = globalThis.localStorage` only when `supportsLocalStorage()` is true, otherwise `memoryLocalStorageAdapter(this.memoryStorage)`. helpers.js:61-90 makes that false in TWO ways: touching `globalThis.localStorage` throws (the variant the comment describes), and — separately — the object is readable but a test write throws (Chrome/Safari "block site data", storage denied for the document). `forgetStoredSession` (supabase-auth.ts:179-191) only ever calls `globalThis.localStorage?.removeItem(storageKey)`, so in the first variant it throws into the catch above and in the second it *succeeds as a no-op on a key that was never written*, with nothing to catch. Either way the session auth-js is actually using is untouched.

(2) The refusal path that leaves a usable refresh token is the pre-flight-refresh path, and on that path auth-js removes nothing either. GoTrueClient.js:3423-3430 (`_signOut` returns `sessionError` before `removeCurrentSession()`), :2540-2590 (`__loadSession` refreshes an expired session and returns `{ session: null, error }` when the access token has really expired), :4290-4313 (`_callRefreshToken` skips `_removeSession()` for a retryable fetch error). So after `adapter.signOut('local')` the session is still in `this.memoryStorage`, with its still-valid refresh token.

(3) `currentSession()` (supabase-auth.ts:386-391) destructures only `data` from `auth.getSession()` and drops the `error`. The refusal was caused by a refresh failure, so the very next `getSession()` hits the same failure — `lastRefreshFailure` is even cached for REFRESH_FAILURE_COOLDOWN_MS (constants.js:21, 60s) — and resolves `{ data: { session: null }, error }`. `currentSession()` maps that to `null`. `stillSignedIn()`'s `catch` (SignOutControl.tsx:73-76, PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:747-749), whose comment says "The session cannot be read, so it cannot be shown as ended either", never runs: auth-js resolves, it does not throw. This is the round-6 defect verbatim — a recovery inside a `catch` the real adapter never enters — moved from PrivacyControlsPage into the adapter's read.

(4) So `open === false` at SignOutControl.tsx:96, and :102-108 navigates to /sign-in carrying `SIGN_OUT_NOT_TOLD_COPY.signInOpen` = "This computer is signed out. …" (packages/contracts/src/account.ts:94-95), rendered as a role="alert" at apps/web/src/pages/auth/SignInPage.tsx:45-49. PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:826-840 takes the same decision and travels to /account-deletion, which prints the same sentence (AccountDeletionPage.tsx:57-61, :81).

(5) The session then comes back, in that same tab. `portalClient` sets `autoRefreshToken: true`; GoTrueClient.js:4738-4753 starts the 30s ticker on a visible tab, and :4680-4707 → `_useSession` → `__loadSession` refreshes from `this.memoryStorage` as soon as the fetch succeeds, writes the rotated session back (`_saveSession`) and emits TOKEN_REFRESHED, which reaches `onChange` (supabase-auth.ts:435-438) and flips `useParentSession` (apps/web/src/lib/session.tsx:81-92) back to `signed_in`. The brand bar on /sign-in carries a "Parent portal" link to /app (apps/web/src/App.tsx:36-40, :167).

The sentence the code proves is "getSession() could not hand back a session at this instant". The sentence the page prints is "This computer is signed out."
findings.impact: A parent on a shared family, school or library computer — in exactly the locked-down browser BUG-322's own recorded impact names — presses Sign out while offline or during an auth outage, reads "This computer is signed out", and leaves. When the network returns the tab's session is refreshed from auth-js's in-memory store and one click on "Parent portal" gives the next person the family's children, homework scans, verdicts, points, safety reports, devices and guardian emails; read screens need no PIN, and the `POST /v1/adult/lock` step-up lock at SignOutControl.tsx:83 failed for the same offline reason, so the parent area is still unlocked too. The same holds for the account-closure flow, where on the `pending` path the sign-in is deliberately still usable until the family purge finishes. The parent has been told something false about their account on the one screen whose job is to tell them the truth about it.
findings.ruled_out: Checked before filing, and none of these makes it a non-issue. (a) The ordinary localStorage case is fine: `forgetStoredSession` really removes the key, `getSession()` then reads empty storage, and nothing can revive it — so this is specific to auth-js's memory storage, not a general claim. (b) `storageKey` cannot be null while the adapter lives: `sessionStorageKey` (supabase-auth.ts:123-129) and supabase-js's own `defaultStorageKey` (SupabaseClient.ts:332) use the same formula, and a URL the former cannot parse also makes `validateSupabaseUrl` (supabase-js helpers.ts:146-162) throw inside `createClient`. (c) auth-js does clear its memory store on the OTHER refusal path — `_signOut`'s server-call branch runs `removeCurrentSession()` → `_removeSession()` (GoTrueClient.js:3432-3446, :4416-4433) — so I confirmed the hole needs the expired-token pre-flight path, and confirmed that path leaves storage alone (:4290-4313). (d) I checked whether anything else clears it: `signOutOnUnauthenticated` (lib/session.tsx:28-40) drops the report but only fires on an HTTP answer, i.e. not while offline; nothing else calls signOut (grep of apps/web/src). (e) I checked whether the existing tests already cover it and they cannot: App.signout.test.tsx:604-628 and :745-774 are the two cases named for blocked storage, and both run on `adapterWith(...)`, a fake whose `getSession` decides `live` for itself (:335-348) — the site-data-blocked stub only makes `forgetStoredSession` throw, it never puts auth-js on its memory store. The real-library block ([HUNT6-F-PREMISE], :400-570) only ever runs with a working localStorage. (f) `window` 'storage' events would not help either: auth-js registers none (only 'visibilitychange', GoTrueClient.js:4735).
findings.reproduction: New case in apps/web/src/App.signout.test.tsx, in its own file so auth-js's module-level `localStorageWriteTests` cache (helpers.js:55-57) is fresh: install a `globalThis.localStorage` whose getter throws a SecurityError (the same stub as :606-612), build the real client through `createSupabaseAuth` so auth-js picks `memoryLocalStorageAdapter`, seed an expired session through the client, and drive `adapter.signOut('local')` with a rejecting fetch. `expect(await adapter.signOut('local')).toEqual({ serverNotTold: true })` and `expect(await adapter.currentSession()).toBeNull()` both pass — that is what makes SignOutControl print "This computer is signed out". Then let the fetch answer `POST /token?grant_type=refresh_token` and advance past REFRESH_FAILURE_COOLDOWN_MS: `expect(await adapter.currentSession()).toBeNull()` goes RED, because the session is back. The paired page-level assertion is in App.signout.test.tsx's WEBR5-E-2 block: after the navigation the notice contains SIGN_OUT_NOT_TOLD_COPY.signInOpen while the adapter can hand out an access token again.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the adapter own the session store instead of guessing at localStorage, and stop spending an unreadable session as an absent one. (1) Add `storage` to `ClientAuthOptions` and hand `portalClient` a small storage object the adapter holds — localStorage when it is readable and writable, otherwise the adapter's own Map — so a refused sign-out can clear whatever auth-js actually used and can say whether it did. (2) Give the adapter a way to report "the session could not be read" distinctly from "there is no session" (keep `error` from `auth.getSession()` in `currentSession()` and surface it), and make both `stillSignedIn()` helpers treat unreadable as still-signed-in, which is what their own comments already say they intend. (3) Only then may either surface print SIGN_OUT_NOT_TOLD_COPY; otherwise show the STILL_OPEN / stillSignedInCopy wording, which is true in that state. Do not weaken any existing assertion: add the memory-storage case beside the [HUNT6-F-PREMISE] block and correct the catch comment at supabase-auth.ts:184-189 to say what it can establish.

findings.title: `serverNotTold: true` is returned for any error auth-js resolves with, including the error that proves the auth service had ALREADY ended the session — so the parent is warned their sign-out never reached the servers about a session the servers destroyed
findings.claim_under_review: "HUNT6-F-3: the report says the SERVER was not told, and only that." (supabase-auth.ts:417) and "WEB-R4-AUTH-2: a sign-out the auth service did not carry out. The server was never told, so the session may still be usable" (apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:74-75)
findings.mechanism: supabase-auth.ts:430-433 is `const { error } = await auth.signOut({ scope }); if (!error) return; forgetStoredSession(storageKey); return { serverNotTold: true };` — every error auth-js resolves with becomes "the server was never told". One class of those errors proves the opposite. GoTrueClient.js:3427-3429 returns `sessionError` from `__loadSession`, and `__loadSession` produces an error whenever a refresh of an expired session fails (:2568-2590) — including a NON-retryable failure, i.e. the auth server rejecting the refresh token. lib/fetch.js:55-88 maps only `session_not_found` to `AuthSessionMissingError` (the one error `_signOut` ignores at :3428); GoTrue answers a revoked or already-used refresh token with `refresh_token_not_found` / `invalid_grant`, which becomes a plain `AuthApiError`. So: access token expired, refresh token revoked server-side (the parent changed their password elsewhere, an admin revoked the session, or the `pending` account closure's family purge has just closed their sign-in) → `_callRefreshToken` gets a 400, calls `_removeSession()` because the access token has really expired (:4306-4312) → `__loadSession` returns `{ session: null, error }` → `_signOut` returns that error → the adapter reports `serverNotTold: true`. `currentSession()` then answers `null`, so `open === false` at SignOutControl.tsx:96, and :102-108 hands SignInPage the notice. Nothing in the adapter distinguishes "we could not reach the server" from "the server refused our credential because it had already ended this session".
findings.impact: A parent whose session the auth service had already destroyed presses Sign out and is told, in a role="alert" above the sign-in form, "We could not tell PencilLift's servers to end the session, so change your password if you are worried" (packages/contracts/src/account.ts:94-95). They are being asked to take a security action over a session that provably no longer exists, and told their sign-out half-failed when it fully succeeded. On the account-closure route the same report travels to /account-deletion (PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:839, AccountDeletionPage.tsx:81), so on the `pending` path a parent reads it on the screen confirming their account deletion — moments after the purge closed the very sign-in whose password they are being told to change.
findings.ruled_out: Checked before filing. (a) I verified auth-js does NOT fold this into the ignorable set: `_signOut` skips only 404/401/403 from `admin.signOut` and `AuthSessionMissingError` (GoTrueClient.js:3428, :3436-3441), and lib/fetch.js:82-86 raises `AuthSessionMissingError` only for the `session_not_found` code, which is what /logout returns, not what /token returns for a bad refresh token. So the refresh-rejection error really does reach the adapter as a plain error. (b) I checked whether the window is unreachable because such a session goes signed-out on its own first: it does eventually — the auto-refresh ticker removes the session and emits SIGNED_OUT once the access token has actually expired — but auth-js's proactive-preserve branch (:4293-4312) keeps the session alive, with no event, for the whole EXPIRY_MARGIN_MS window while the refresh is already failing, and `_callRefreshToken`'s 60s failure cache (:4204-4210, constants.js:21) returns the cached failure without removing anything, so the control is still on screen and pressable. (c) I checked the copy is really shown on this path and not suppressed: SignOutControl's early return at :67 hides the control but not the navigation at :108, and SignInPage.tsx:45-49 renders the notice from router state regardless of session state. (d) The over-warning is in the cautious direction — no data is exposed — which is why this is medium and not high.
findings.reproduction: In apps/web/src/App.signout.test.tsx's `WEB-R4-AUTH-2 the Supabase adapter surfaces a refused sign-out` block, a case over `adapterWith({ error: { message: 'Invalid Refresh Token: Refresh Token Not Found', code: 'refresh_token_not_found' } })` asserting `expect(await adapter.signOut('local')).toBeUndefined()` — i.e. a server that answered and destroyed the session is not reported as a server that was never told — goes red today, because the adapter answers `{ serverNotTold: true }` for every error shape. The page-level form belongs beside the WEBR5-E-2 case: after that refusal the notice must not contain "We could not tell PencilLift's servers to end the session".
findings.suggested_fix: Report the refusal from the fact that the server was not reached, not from "auth-js returned something". In the adapter's signOut, inspect the error before reporting: an error that came from the auth server rejecting the session's own credential (a 400/404 refresh-token or session error) means the session is already ended, so resolve with nothing to report after `forgetStoredSession`; keep `{ serverNotTold: true }` for a transport failure or a 5xx, which are the cases the parent's warning exists for. Correct the two docstrings (auth.ts:73-96, supabase-auth.ts:417-420) to say what the report is derived from. Do not widen `SignOutReport` beyond `void | SignOutRefused` unless the lead wants a third outcome.

findings.title: The adapter's hand-removal of the stored session raises no SIGNED_OUT and no cross-tab broadcast, so a second open portal tab keeps the family's page and a live signed-in state after the parent has been told this computer is signed out
findings.claim_under_review: "`this.storage` is `globalThis.localStorage` whenever `supportsLocalStorage()` is true — so removing that key removes what `getSession()` reads." (supabase-auth.ts:171-173) and "This browser IS signed out, so the portal leaves, and the notice travels with it." (apps/web/src/components/SignOutControl.tsx:106-107)
findings.mechanism: `forgetStoredSession` (supabase-auth.ts:179-191) removes the session with a bare `globalThis.localStorage.removeItem(storageKey)`. That is the only removal on the refusal path, and it bypasses auth-js's own teardown: `_removeSession()` (GoTrueClient.js:4416-4433) is the only place a removal raises `SIGNED_OUT`, and `_notifyAllSubscribers` (:4345-4354) is what posts it on the per-storageKey BroadcastChannel that every `persistSession` client in every tab holds (:270-291). auth-js registers no `window` 'storage' listener (only 'visibilitychange', :4735), and `_recoverAndRefresh` on a visibility change returns without an event when storage is already empty (:4084, :4114-4119). The portal's only trigger for re-reading the session is that event stream: `useParentSession` (apps/web/src/lib/session.tsx:81-92) reads once on mount and then only from `auth.onChange`, which is `auth.onAuthStateChange` (supabase-auth.ts:435-438). So a second portal tab is never told. It keeps `{ status: 'signed_in', session }` and keeps its already-rendered page on screen — `RequireParent` (lib/session.tsx:117-130) re-reads only when it remounts. The asymmetry is the defect: a sign-out auth-js CARRIES OUT notifies the other tab (`_removeSession` → SIGNED_OUT → broadcast → that tab drops to SignInPrompt), while a sign-out it REFUSES, where the adapter removes the session by hand, does not.
findings.impact: A parent with the portal open in two tabs (a very ordinary shape — Children in one, Homework or Privacy & data in the other) presses Sign out in one, is told "This computer is signed out", and walks away from a shared family, school or library computer. The other tab still shows the family's children, homework scans, verdicts, points, safety reports, devices and guardian emails, and still says "Signed in as p•••@example.test" — read screens need no PIN, which is the whole reason WEB-R2-01 exists. Through the account-closure flow it is worse: the account is already closed, and the second tab keeps displaying the family it belongs to.
findings.ruled_out: Checked before filing. (a) The BroadcastChannel really exists in both tabs and really would have carried the event: GoTrueClient.js:270-273 creates it whenever `isBrowser() && BroadcastChannel && persistSession && storageKey`, which the portal client satisfies (supabase-auth.ts:131-141), and the handler at :277-291 re-notifies local subscribers — so the loss is caused by skipping `_removeSession`, not by an absent channel. (b) I checked for another path that would wake the second tab and found none: no 'storage' listener in auth-js; `_recoverAndRefresh` on visibilitychange emits nothing over empty storage; the auto-refresh tick reads empty storage and returns (:4686-4690); `signOutOnUnauthenticated` (lib/session.tsx:28-40) only fires if that tab makes a request and gets UNAUTHENTICATED, which needs a user action. (c) I checked the exposure is not merely theoretical state: `useApiQuery` (lib/session.tsx:138-166) holds loaded data in component state, and the second tab's components stay mounted, so the data stays painted. (d) I checked the one-tab case is already handled — SignOutControl navigates with `{ replace: true }` and the portal pages unmount — so this is specifically the cross-tab gap. (e) I checked there is no cached family in browser storage for the next person to read: the only auth-bearing key in apps/web/src is auth-js's (grep of localStorage/sessionStorage/indexedDB), the RouteError marker is not sensitive.
findings.reproduction: A new case in apps/web/src/App.signout.test.tsx over `adapterWith({ error: { message: 'Failed to fetch' } })`: register a second `auth.onChange` listener (standing in for the other tab's `useParentSession`) before calling `adapter.signOut('local')`, then assert the listener was called — it is not today, so `expect(listener).toHaveBeenCalled()` goes red. The page-level form is a two-router render where the second router stays on /app/children: after the first one's Sign out it still shows "Page /app/children" and "Signed in as p•••@example.test", so `expect(screen.queryByText(/Signed in as/)).toBeNull()` goes red.
findings.suggested_fix: After the hand-removal on the refusal path, let auth-js perform its own teardown so the event and the broadcast go out: with the stored session now gone, a second `await auth.signOut({ scope })` takes the token-less path (GoTrueClient.js:3423-3430 sees no sessionError and no access token) straight to `removeCurrentSession()` → `_removeSession()`, which raises SIGNED_OUT and broadcasts it, and resolves `{ error: null }`. The first call's refusal must still be the reported outcome — the second call is teardown only and must not turn `{ serverNotTold: true }` into `undefined`, and it must not be allowed to re-enter the refusal path (it will still refuse in the memory-storage case of HUNT7-F-1, which is fine as long as the report is not recomputed). Assert the event on the adapter, and keep every existing assertion.

findings.title: The claim round 6 deleted from auth.ts as false — that the adapter clears this origin's storage on a refusal — survives verbatim in SignOutControl, in the docstring and on the branch that prints "This computer is signed out"
findings.claim_under_review: "On the refusal path the adapter clears this origin's storage itself" (SignOutControl.tsx:56) and "WEBR5-E-2: the adapter cleared this browser, but the server was never told." (SignOutControl.tsx:103)
findings.mechanism: BUG-322/HUNT6-F-3 was filed and closed on exactly this sentence: apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:73-93 no longer says "this browser's stored session has been removed", because `forgetStoredSession` is best-effort — it returns silently when `storageKey` is null, swallows any throw (supabase-auth.ts:179-191), and, as round 6's own comment at supabase-auth.ts:166-169 states, is "a no-op" on the server-call refusal path where auth-js had already removed the session. The removal of that claim is incomplete: the same assertion is still stated as fact in the file the round-6 diff edited. :56 says the adapter clears this origin's storage on "the refusal path" (singular — and on one of the two paths it is auth-js, not the adapter, that clears anything; on the other the adapter only tries), and :103 asserts "the adapter cleared this browser" on a branch where the code knows only that `currentSession()` resolved `null`, which is the weaker fact HUNT7-F-1 turns on. This is the prose a next author reads to argue the re-read away, which is the stated reason (L-053) the auth.ts wording was corrected at all.
findings.impact: The one surviving statement of a claim two rounds have now shown false sits next to the code that prints "This computer is signed out" to a parent, and reads as a licence to delete the `open` re-read at :96 as redundant. Round 6's own hunt found the previous author doing precisely that in PrivacyControlsPage.
findings.ruled_out: Checked before filing. (a) I confirmed the code does NOT depend on the false sentence: :96 computes `open` unconditionally before either navigate, so the behaviour is driven by the read, not by the comment — which is why this is low and not a correctness finding. (b) I confirmed the sentence is false rather than merely loose, on both refusal paths, by reading `_signOut` (GoTrueClient.js:3422-3452): the server-call branch runs `removeCurrentSession()` itself, so there the adapter clears nothing; the pre-flight branch leaves storage alone, so there the adapter's attempt is the only removal and it can fail silently (supabase-auth.ts:179-191). (c) I checked this is not already recorded as a residual for BUG-322 in docs/Bug_Ledger.md:343 — that row's CHECKER cell is about the adapter keeping option (b) and the callers reading the session; SignOutControl's docstring is not named. (d) I checked the sibling surface: PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:780-813 was rewritten in this diff and does not carry the claim.
findings.reproduction: Prose, so no runtime assertion. The mechanical check is that `grep -n "clears this origin\|the adapter cleared this browser" apps/web/src` still returns SignOutControl.tsx:56 and :103 at 5ba16c3, while the identical claim was removed from apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts in the same commit (git diff b802686 5ba16c3 -- apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts).
findings.suggested_fix: Say what the branch knows. At :56 state that on the refusal path this origin's stored session may have been cleared — by auth-js on the server-call path, best-effort by the adapter on the pre-flight path — and that which of the two happened is not reported, which is why :96 reads the session. At :103 replace "the adapter cleared this browser" with what was established: this browser has no readable session, and the server was never told. Keep the cross-reference to auth.ts:73-93 so the two files state one rule.

findings.title: `forgetStoredSession`'s new docstring says a refusal leaves a stored session on "exactly one path" and excuses the storage-changed case as having nothing to remove; there is a second path, and on it the function removes a session auth-js deliberately preserved
findings.claim_under_review: "…which in the pinned @supabase/auth-js 2.116.0 is exactly one path: the stored access token has ALREADY EXPIRED…" (supabase-auth.ts:144-152) and "(auth-js also drops the fallback when storage changed under the refresh, but then the stored session is already gone and this has nothing to remove.)" (supabase-auth.ts:161-163)
findings.mechanism: `__loadSession`'s proactive-preserve branch (GoTrueClient.js:2568-2590) hands the stored session back with `error: null` only when the access token is still valid AND `stillStored && stillStored.refresh_token === currentSession.refresh_token`. The guard fails in two ways, not one: storage was CLEARED, and storage was REPLACED — another tab's refresh rotated the slot (`_saveSession` after a successful `_callRefreshToken`, :4265-4272). In the replaced case `__loadSession` returns `{ session: null, error }` although storage holds a newer, perfectly valid session; `_signOut` returns that as `sessionError` at :3427-3429 with no removal; and the adapter then calls `forgetStoredSession`, which removes that valid session. So (i) the refusal-without-clearing case is not "exactly one path" and does not require an expired access token, and (ii) the parenthetical's "the stored session is already gone and this has nothing to remove" is false for the replaced half — the function has a live session to remove, and removes it. The same wrong enumeration is repeated in the test docstring at apps/web/src/App.signout.test.tsx:427-431.
findings.impact: No user is harmed by the removal itself — the parent pressed Sign out, so ending the session is the intended outcome — but the enumeration is what a fixer reads to decide which paths need a removal at all, and it currently tells them one path exists where two do. It also hides the cross-tab consequence of HUNT7-F-3: on this path the removal takes out a session the OTHER tab is actively using, again with no SIGNED_OUT.
findings.ruled_out: Checked before filing. (a) I confirmed the replaced-storage case is real and distinct by reading the guard at GoTrueClient.js:2585-2588 and the rotation write at :4265-4272; the debug line at :4250 even distinguishes `nowHolds: 'replaced'` from `'cleared'`, so the library itself treats them as two outcomes. (b) I confirmed the outcome is not a user-facing wrong answer: after the removal `getSession()` reads empty storage, so `currentSession()` is null and "This computer is signed out" is true in that tab — which is why this is low and filed as prose, not as a correctness bug. (c) I checked that this is not the same sentence as HUNT7-F-4: that one is SignOutControl's claim about who cleared the storage; this one is the adapter docstring's enumeration of when there is anything to clear. (d) I checked the two-tab precondition is reachable: each tab gets its own GoTrueClient with the same storage key and no lock on the default path (GoTrueClient.js:3413-3420), so their refreshes are not serialized.
findings.reproduction: Prose plus a characterization gap. The case that would show it belongs in App.signout.test.tsx's [HUNT6-F-PREMISE] block, beside [HUNT6-F-MARGIN]: a real client with an unexpired token inside EXPIRY_MARGIN_MS whose storage is rewritten with a different `refresh_token` while the pre-flight refresh is failing. `expect(localStorage.getItem(STORED)).not.toBeNull()` after `adapter.signOut('local')` — which is what "this has nothing to remove" predicts — goes red: the adapter removed the replacement.
findings.suggested_fix: State both paths. Say that a refusal leaves a stored session whenever `__loadSession` returns a `sessionError`, which is (i) an access token that has really expired and a refresh that failed, and (ii) an access token still inside the margin whose refresh failed while another writer replaced the stored slot — and that in case (ii) the session `forgetStoredSession` removes is a valid one, so the removal is intended but is also the cross-tab removal that raises no SIGNED_OUT. Correct the matching sentence in App.signout.test.tsx:427-431. Do not remove or weaken the [HUNT6-F-MARGIN] case; add the replaced-storage case beside it.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: assuranceLevel() returns `null` exactly when no level was read, and never as a stand-in for aal1 (the HUNT6-F-2 change, supabase-auth.ts:353-357).
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: I read GoTrueClient._getAuthenticatorAssuranceLevel (GoTrueClient.js:5042-5091) to see every value it can resolve with, and looked for (a) a real level that `!data.currentLevel` would swallow, (b) an unreadable level that still slips through as 'aal1', and (c) the same wrapper-vs-field gap in the sibling lookup. I then enumerated every consumer (`grep -rn assuranceLevel apps/web/src packages`) rather than trusting the two the tests name.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: `currentLevel` is only ever 'aal1' | 'aal2' | null, so `!data.currentLevel` cannot swallow a real answer, and the two branches that mean "nothing was read" — no session (:5073-5078) and a JWT with no `aal` claim (:5081-5084) — both produce `currentLevel: null` with `error: null`, which the new guard now catches. The sibling `verifiedTotpFactorId()` has no symmetric hole: `_listFactors` (:5010-5030) always builds `totp: []`, so `data.totp.find` cannot throw and a failure always arrives as `{ data: null, error }`. There are exactly two consumers, MfaPage.tsx:39-42 and PinResetPage.tsx:73-78, and both map `null` to a refusal that offers nothing — including the sharp case of an unreadable level beside a verified factor, which is what would otherwise have run the session-replacing password grant with no two-step step.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: SignOutControl never reaches the "This computer is signed out" notice without first reading the session (the L-037 rule that the pre-check is on every path, not only the enumerated one).
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: I traced every exit from `signOut()` at SignOutControl.tsx:79-112 looking for a path that reaches the notice with `stillSignedIn()` skipped — the shape of the round-6 HIGH, where PrivacyControlsPage gated the read on a variable only the `catch` set. I also checked whether the early return at :67 (`state.status !== 'signed_in'`) could unmount the work mid-flight and let the navigation run with `open` unresolved, and whether a successful sign-out's SIGNED_OUT event could reorder the two.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: `const open = await stillSignedIn()` at :96 is unconditional and precedes both navigations; `refused` is a plain boolean and no branch bypasses the read. The early return only makes the component render nothing — the running async function keeps its closure, and both `setProblem` and `navigate` still execute. So the enumerated case and the fall-through take the same check. (What the check *establishes* is a different matter — see HUNT7-F-1 — but the round-6 structural fix itself is sound, and PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:826 now matches it.)

properties_attacked_and_held.property: A refusal is reported as a value and never as a rejection, so the account-closure caller still reaches the page that explains the closure (ACC-WEB-AUTH-A).
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: I looked for anything on the adapter's signOut path that can throw rather than resolve: `closeRecovery()` (supabase-auth.ts:399), `auth.signOut({ scope })` (:430), and `forgetStoredSession` (:432) with storage made hostile. For the last one I checked whether `globalThis.localStorage?.removeItem` can throw *outside* the try — the optional chain is evaluated after the property access, so a throwing getter is inside it — and whether a SecurityError from merely touching localStorage escapes.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: `closeRecovery` is a field assignment; `auth.signOut` resolves with `{ error }` on every failure auth-js knows (GoTrueClient.js:3412-3452, and the `AuthError` catches in lib/fetch.js); and `forgetStoredSession`'s try/catch (supabase-auth.ts:181-190) covers the getter access, so even a browser that throws on touching localStorage gets `{ serverNotTold: true }` rather than a rejection. Both production callers keep a `catch` as well (SignOutControl.tsx:91-95, PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:819-825), and the contract is asserted on the adapter directly, which is the right place now that no caller is catch-free.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: The two surfaces that say the not-told sentence cannot drift apart (SIGN_OUT_NOT_TOLD_COPY, packages/contracts/src/account.ts:66-102).
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: I grepped every reference to the constant and checked, for each surface that renders it, that the test asserting it renders the REAL page and compares against the constant rather than a regex over part of the string (L-054). I also checked the round-6 correction that the mobile app is not a third sharer, by looking for an import of the constant outside apps/web.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: SignOutControl.tsx:32 and AccountDeletionPage.tsx:57-61 are the only renderers, both read the constant, and both are asserted against it where they render — App.signout.test.tsx:257 over the real SignInPage, PrivacyControlsPage.test.tsx:1373/1391 over the real public page — with the closed/open split pinned separately. Nothing outside apps/web imports it, so the round-6 correction is accurate. One residual over-claim worth noting rather than filing: the contracts docstring says "a surface that inlined its own sentence would turn a test red", which is only true of a *paraphrase* — a byte-identical inline copy would still pass `toContain`. The test comment at App.signout.test.tsx:258-259 states it correctly.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: The inverted tests would go red if the round-6 fix were reverted (the lead's instruction on BUG-323).
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: I took each inverted assertion in turn and asked what production change would turn it red: the PrivacyControlsPage pair, and the three in my own files ([HUNT6-F-MARGIN] at App.signout.test.tsx:522-531, [HUNT6-F-REFUTED] at :545-553, and the [HUNT6-F-3] adapter case at :604-628). I checked each against the fake or the real library it runs on.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: It holds where it matters: the two `keepsSessionOnSignOut` closure cases (:687-712, :745-774) supply a readable session and assert the parent stays on /app/privacy, so restoring the `unverified &&` gate turns them red, and the ledger records that mutation. It does NOT hold for the three inverted assertions in my own files — [HUNT6-F-MARGIN] and [HUNT6-F-REFUTED] characterize auth-js and would pass with any production revert, and the [HUNT6-F-3] adapter case asserts `currentSession()` is null over a fake that flips `live` itself. That is defensible, because the round-6 change those cases accompany is comments, and their job is to establish the library facts the comments rest on. But it is also exactly why HUNT7-F-1 is invisible: the two cases named for a site-data-blocked browser never put auth-js on its memory storage, so the fact they claim to pin is decided by the fake.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: Every surface that signs out makes the same check and says the same true thing (L-037 / L-057).
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: I enumerated the callers rather than trusting the two the brief names: `grep -rn signOut apps/web/src` for production code, then read each — SignOutControl, PrivacyControlsPage's closure, `signOutOnUnauthenticated` (lib/session.tsx:28-40), the password-proof client's own sign-out (supabase-auth.ts:312-318) — and checked separately for a step-up or MFA sign-out and for any other place a "signed out" sentence is printed (`grep -rn "signed out" apps/web/src`).
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: There are four callers and no fifth: nothing in StepUpPrompt or MfaPage signs out. The two that present a signed-out screen both read the session first. `signOutOnUnauthenticated` drops the report, but it prints no claim of its own — RequireParent's SignInPrompt is driven by its own `currentSession()` read (lib/session.tsx:117-130) — and it only fires on an HTTP answer, so it cannot be the offline refusal path. The proof client persists nothing and its failed sign-out leaves nothing behind. The remaining "…this device is signed out" strings (ACCOUNT_CLOSE_COPY) are kept off the survived-session path by `stillSignedInCopy` (PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:723-729), which is the HUNT5-N6 fix and still holds.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: No local state a next person could read survives a refused sign-out in the tab that performed it.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: I grepped every browser-storage use in apps/web/src (localStorage / sessionStorage / indexedDB), checked for a module-level query or family cache, checked what `useParentSession` and `useApiQuery` hold and when they are torn down, checked the recovery grant, and checked that the notice navigation cannot be walked back into the portal with Back.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: The only auth-bearing key in the web app is auth-js's own; there is no shared query cache (`useApiQuery` state dies with its component, lib/session.tsx:138-166); the recovery grant is closed before the call (supabase-auth.ts:399) and cannot be re-opened without a PASSWORD_RECOVERY event; the PKCE verifier is useless without a code; and both navigations use `{ replace: true }`, so the /app entry is gone from history. The tab that signed out is clean. The two ways state does survive are filed: auth-js's in-memory store (HUNT7-F-1) and a second tab that is never told (HUNT7-F-3).

properties_attacked_and_held.property: The key the adapter removes is always the key auth-js reads (sessionStorageKey, supabase-auth.ts:117-141).
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: I compared `sessionStorageKey`'s formula with supabase-js's own `defaultStorageKey` (SupabaseClient.ts:331-332) and then attacked the null branch: a URL that `new URL` cannot parse would give a null key, make `forgetStoredSession` a silent no-op, and leave auth-js using a key the adapter never touches — a refresh token left in localStorage on every refusal.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: The formulas are identical, and `portalClient` passes the key explicitly, so the two cannot diverge even for a custom auth hostname. The null branch cannot coexist with a live adapter: the same parse failure makes `validateSupabaseUrl` (supabase-js lib/helpers.ts:146-162) throw inside `createClient`, so `createSupabaseAuth` never returns an adapter with a null storage key.

findings.title: The pairing-code panel — including round 6's new 'stale' state — replaces the card's only ActionFeedback, so a STEP_UP_REQUIRED refusal of "Activate X again" renders nothing at all
findings.claim_under_review: "Create a new one if {child.nickname} is active again — the notice above says whether that is possible." (ChildrenPage.tsx:542-543), together with StepUpPrompt's own stated property: "the parent enters the PIN here, on the page they were already filling in — following a link to /app/security would unmount the form" (apps/web/src/components/StepUpPrompt.tsx:9-11, WEB-R2-05).
findings.mechanism: ChildrenPage.tsx:526-565 is one three-way ternary: `code === null ? <ActionFeedback/> : code === 'stale' ? <stale notice> : <PairingCodePanel/>`. ActionFeedback (SecurityPage.tsx:79-96) is the ONLY renderer of this card's `feedback`, and the only place StepUpNotice -> StepUpPrompt (components/StepUpPrompt.tsx:37) can appear; the separate notice at ChildrenPage.tsx:517 covers exactly one rule (CHILD_ACTIVATION_RULES.consentRequired) and only when lastAction === 'activate'. So whenever `code !== null`, every outcome of activate(), archive(), saveProfile() and createCode() is discarded: the success line, the ErrorState for a business rule or a network failure, and the inline PIN field for STEP_UP_REQUIRED. Round 6 made that window reachable with no press on this card, and permanent: the new effect at ChildrenPage.tsx:244-250 sets `code` to 'stale' the moment `pairingRedeemable` goes false, and nothing clears 'stale' except the parent pressing Done at :545-554. That state exists exactly in the states whose only offered control is "Activate {nickname} again" (:420-431), and POST /v1/children/:childId/activate calls assertRecentUnlock (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:462) while an unlock lasts only "a few minutes" (SecurityPage.tsx:179) — so STEP_UP_REQUIRED is the routine outcome of that press, and the card shows nothing: useAction clears busy in its finally (SecurityPage.tsx:57-59), so the only trace is the label flickering "Activating…" and back.
findings.impact: A parent whose archived child is holding a stale pairing code presses "Activate Riley again", and the page does nothing at all: no PIN field, no error, no link to Security, no success line. The archived child cannot be brought back from that card until the parent finds the Done button or reloads the page — and WEBR4-01 exists precisely because an archived child with no way back loses their device access. The same is true of a NO_FREE_SLOT or network refusal, and of the success message after a re-activation that did work.
findings.ruled_out: (a) The pre-round-6 code had the same suppression for a real code panel (`{code ? <PairingCodePanel/> : <ActionFeedback/>}`), so I checked whether round 6 widened it. It did: 'stale' is entered by a RELOAD with no press on this card (:244-250), persists until Done, and exists only in the states where "Activate again" is the offered control — the round turned an after-you-pressed-a-button window into a standing one, under new copy that invites the very press it swallows. (b) I checked for a second feedback renderer on the card: the consent notice at :517-525 fires only for `activationError?.rule === CHILD_ACTIVATION_RULES.consentRequired`, and `activationError` is null unless lastAction === 'activate' (:336-337); nothing else renders feedback. (c) I checked whether this is the portal's normal pattern: `grep ActionFeedback apps/web/src` shows ChildrenPage.tsx:527 is the ONLY conditional render site — Devices (:171), Guardians (:139/267/312/378), Family (:125/518/602), Support, Security and all five learning sections render it as an unconditional sibling. (d) I checked whether the parent can recover elsewhere: /app/security exists, but StepUpPrompt's docstring records following a link there as the defect WEB-R2-05 was filed to remove, and the card renders no such link. (e) I checked that the round-4 property is genuinely pinned elsewhere and passes only by luck here: ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx:158-173 asserts findByLabelText('Parent PIN') for this exact button on an archived card, and passes only because `code` is null in that case.
findings.reproduction: apps/web/src/pages/app/ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx, `[G-PROSE] one status change closes every open panel, and clears it > clears the archive confirmation rather than hiding it, so it cannot reopen itself` (:620-646). Make servingApi's `send` reject `/activate` with `new ApiRequestError('STEP_UP_REQUIRED','Enter your parent PIN',403)` and add after the click at :640 `expect(await within(archived).findByLabelText('Parent PIN')).toBeTruthy()` — red today, green in the sibling case at :170 where no code is held. Success-side variant, also red today: after :642 add `expect(within(back).getByText(/uses one of your paid slots/)).toBeTruthy()`.
findings.suggested_fix: Render ActionFeedback unconditionally on the card — it already returns null for a null feedback (SecurityPage.tsx:86) — and make the code / stale panel a separate sibling below it, so no panel can be the reason a refusal is invisible. Keep the consentRequired substitution at :517 exactly as it is. Note when writing the test that the stale notice also carries role="status", so a `getByRole('status')` assertion would become ambiguous; assert on the message text.

findings.title: The new concurrent-change notice says "Another guardian changed …" for any difference between the live prop and the seed — including the reader's own change, and a guardian who does not exist
findings.claim_under_review: "Another guardian changed {drifted.join(' and ')} while this form was open." (ChildrenPage.tsx:724 and FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:294), and the docstrings that justify it: "What another guardian changed while this form was open: the live prop against the seed (HUNT6-G-8)" (ChildrenPage.tsx:643-645, FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:222-225).
findings.mechanism: `drifted` (ChildrenPage.tsx:647-653; FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:226-229) is a pure comparison of the live prop against the mount-time seed. Nothing in the data says who wrote the new value: familyChildSchema and familyOverviewResponseSchema are strictObjects with no actor field (packages/contracts/src/family.ts:66-92) and GET /v1/family selects no actor column (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:186-249) — the very fact that made this same diff rewrite the deletion notice to name the open request instead of the reader (ChildrenPage.tsx:364-369; HUNT6-I-3 on mobile). Two reachable writers that are not another guardian. (1) The reader on a second surface: the phone app PATCHes the same child from apps/mobile/app/(parent)/children.tsx:374, and this card is keyed on child.id so the open form is never remounted; any sibling action's reload then lands the reader's own value under it as "drift". A second portal tab does the same. (2) The reader's own SAVE whose reload failed — the flow WEBR4-04 built and the page's own test walks: the PATCH succeeds, the GET fails, useLastGood (SecurityPage.tsx:102-109) keeps the pre-save values on screen beside "Try again", the parent reopens the form and is reseeded from those stale values, and the next successful GET lands their own new name/grade as drift. In a family with one adult the sentence additionally asserts that a second guardian exists: neither page reads /v1/guardians and neither has a guardian count.
findings.impact: A parent is told in bold that another adult changed their child's grade, nickname or age band, or the family's time zone, when nobody did — most often when they changed it themselves seconds earlier on the phone, and possibly with their own "Saved. Your family is …" confirmation still on screen next to it. For a single-guardian family the notice asserts that another adult has write access to the child's profile, a claim about account security the page cannot support. It is the mirror image of the defect this diff fixed twice (G-I3-WEB on the web, HUNT6-I-3 on mobile): a notice naming an actor the response cannot establish.
findings.ruled_out: (a) I checked whether the response can carry the actor: it cannot — both schemas are strict with no such field, the route selects none, and the audit trail records changed field NAMES only (docs/Bug_Ledger.md BUG-181) and is not exposed to the portal. (b) I checked whether reseeding the form would remove the drift instead: it would re-introduce BUG-330 (the value the parent can see becoming unsavable), so I am NOT proposing that; only the actor claim is at issue. (c) I checked whether the reader's own save closes the form first, which would kill case (2): it does (ChildrenPage.tsx:330, FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:120) — but the parent reopens it while the failed-reload retry is still on screen, which is exactly what FamilyDashboardPage.save.test.tsx:169 does, and the seed is then the stale last-good rather than the value just saved. (d) I checked whether the system writes these fields, so as not to over-claim: releaseSlotlessProfiles (apps/api/src/services/billing-sync.ts:1314-1324) changes `status` only, and `drifted` does not compare status. (e) I checked why the existing tests miss it: both fakes leave the served overview unmutated by the PATCH (ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx:85-93, FamilyDashboardPage.save.test.tsx:88-91), so the reader's own save can never appear in a later GET.
findings.reproduction: apps/web/src/pages/app/FamilyDashboardPage.save.test.tsx, `[HUNT5-F-1] … > does not put the stale time zone back when a retry lands the other guardian's change` (:149-191). Make the fake's PATCH mutate the family it serves, as the server does, so the third GET returns `displayName: 'The Riveras'` as well as `timezone: 'Europe/Berlin'`; then `expect(screen.queryByText(/another guardian changed the family name/i)).toBeNull()` is red today. The same one-line change to ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx's `later` overview (have the PATCH move the served nickname) reproduces it for the child form.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the actor and keep everything the data supports: "The grade was changed to Grade 4 somewhere else while this form was open." / "This family's time zone was changed to Europe/Berlin somewhere else while this form was open." — followed by the existing two sentences about which fields the form will and will not send. If the product wants to name an actor, GET /v1/family has to carry one, which is a contract and route change rather than a copy change. Then extend ArchivedChildCopy.test.tsx's portal-wide actor sweep so no portal copy attributes a change to an adult the response does not name.

findings.title: HUNT6-G-2's "one helper decides the sentence for every surface" stopped at the web: both mobile parent screens still print "Archived: history only" for a child whose history the purge is deleting, and the home screen has no notice to correct it
findings.claim_under_review: "the branch lives in the one helper both surfaces print from (L-037)" and "HUNT6-G-2: the flag is tested FIRST, before the status, exactly as `childPickerSuffix` above and the controls below already test it" (apps/web/src/pages/app/ChildrenPage.tsx:84-90), plus the lead's own round-6 decision: "give childStatusLabel the deletionPending branch, and sweep the other printers the finding names — RewardsPage and the mobile family view — in the same pass."
findings.mechanism: childStatusText (apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.ts:54-62) takes only `FamilyChild['status']` and returns 'Archived: history only' for 'archived'; childRows sets `statusText: childStatusText(child.status)` at :129 with no deletionPending branch, and ChildRow carries no such field (:84). public.request_deletion archives a child-scope target in the same transaction (supabase/migrations/0890_*.sql: `update public.child_profiles set status = 'archived', archived_at = now() where id = p_child`), so every deletion-pending child on these screens is 'archived'. Two printers consume it: apps/mobile/app/(parent)/children.tsx:224 `Status: {row.statusText}` — which at least renders the "Data deletion under way" notice at :245-258 below it, so the screen says both things at once — and apps/mobile/app/(parent)/home.tsx:94 `Status: {row.statusText}`, where `grep -n 'deletion' home.tsx` returns nothing: that screen renders the bold claim that the history is kept with no counter-notice anywhere. home.tsx:94 is the structural twin of the web dashboard row HUNT5-F-2 fixed and ChildrenPage.tsx:355 that HUNT6-G-2 fixed. The round-6 ledger row for this fix (docs/Bug_Ledger.md BUG-324) documents the RewardsPage half as refuted in its residual column and does not mention the mobile family view at all, so this case was dropped silently rather than recorded.
findings.impact: A parent who has asked for one child's data to be deleted opens the phone app's home screen and reads, in the status line for that child, that their history is kept and available — while the purge job enqueued in the same transaction is deleting it. On the Children screen they read that and the opposite notice on the same card. This is the exact sentence the product has now paid to remove twice (HUNT5-F-2, HUNT6-G-2) and it is still the default on the surface most parents use.
findings.ruled_out: (a) I checked that the flag actually reaches these screens: GET /v1/family returns `deletionPending` for every child (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:243), the mobile screens parse the full familyOverviewResponseSchema (not a local z.object that would strip it — the HUNT5-F-2/BUG-274 failure mode), and children.tsx:139 already reads `child.deletionPending === true`, so the data is present and only the label ignores it. (b) I checked whether a family-scope request could be the only reachable case, which would make it unreachable: no — a child-scope request is the reachable one and it archives the child, and a family-scope request revokes every membership so the screen shows its no-family notice instead (recorded for children.tsx at :236-244). (c) I checked the ledger before filing: BUG-324's residual column refutes only RewardsPage (correctly — GET /v1/rewards drops such a child via notBeingDeleted, and RewardsPage.tsx:400-408 carries that justification in a comment); nothing anywhere records the mobile label as accepted-open. (d) I checked whether a mobile test pins the wrong behaviour: apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.test.ts:39/45 assert statusText for active and draft only, and no case passes deletionPending, so the branch is simply absent rather than deliberately tested.
findings.reproduction: apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.test.ts — add a case beside the existing statusText assertions at :39/:45: `expect(childRows(familyWith({...archivedChild, deletionPending: true}))[0]!.statusText).toBe('Data deletion under way')`. Red today (it returns 'Archived: history only').
