findings.suggested_fix: Give childStatusText the same shape as the web helper — take `{status, deletionPending?}` and return 'Data deletion under way' before the status switch — and pass the child rather than the status at family-view.ts:129, so both mobile printers (children.tsx:224 and home.tsx:94) are corrected by the one helper, which is what HUNT6-G-2's own claim says. Add the family-view.test.ts case above so the branch cannot go dead again, and record in BUG-324's row that the mobile half is now done.

findings.title: Three rounds of fixes gave the web "send only the fields the parent edited"; the phone's child form still PATCHes all three fields from its mount-time seed, so a nickname fix on the phone reverts the other guardian's grade
findings.claim_under_review: "Only the fields the parent changed are sent, so a concurrent edit by the other guardian is not overwritten wholesale" (apps/web/src/pages/app/ChildrenPage.tsx:571-573) and the mobile form's own docstring "Correcting one child's nickname, grade and age band (WEB-R2-03) … The server re-checks the recent PIN unlock, the contract bounds and the archived rule" (apps/mobile/app/(parent)/children.tsx:348-352), which asserts the same WEB-R2-03 behaviour as the web form it was written from.
findings.mechanism: apps/mobile/app/(parent)/children.tsx EditChild seeds its fields from the live prop once (`useState(child.nickname)` at :362, :363, :364) and submits `onSave({ nickname: name, gradeLevel: Number(grade), ageBand })` at :374 — all three fields, unconditionally, from that seed. saveProfile (:195-222) sends that body straight to PATCH /v1/children/:id, whose schema accepts any subset (packages/contracts/src/family.ts:110-120) and whose route writes exactly the fields present. The card is keyed on row.id (children.tsx:94-101) so a reload never remounts it, and EditChild only unmounts when `editing` flips false (:301), so the seed is from whenever the form was opened. No reload is even needed for the loss: guardian B moves Riley to grade 4 on the portal while parent A has the phone form open on grade 3, A fixes a typo in the nickname and presses Save, and the PATCH carries gradeLevel 3. That is BUG-222/WEBR4-03 verbatim; the web fixed it in round 4, HUNT5-F-1 fixed the seed in round 5 and HUNT6-G-8 replaced the diff with `touched` in this round — all three inside apps/web only, and the round-6 fix plan's HUNT6-G-8 entry names no mobile file.
findings.impact: A parent correcting a nickname on the phone silently puts their child back in last year's grade — the value new practice generation is pitched at (ChildrenPage.tsx:719, children.tsx:404) — or back into the previous age band, which sets the reading level of everything the child is shown. Nothing on either screen says it happened. This is the harm the product has now filed and fixed three times on one surface while the other surface kept it.
findings.ruled_out: (a) I checked for a guard on the API side that would stop it: PATCH /v1/children/:childId accepts any non-empty subset and applies what it is given; the contract's refine only rejects an empty body, so a wholesale write is a valid request and there is no server-side last-write detection. (b) I checked whether the mobile form is unreachable or read-only for the affected children: it is offered for every non-archived, non-deletion-pending child (children.tsx:291-302), i.e. exactly the children whose grade matters. (c) I checked whether the phone form reseeds on reload, which would have shrunk the window: it does not — key={row.id} plus a mount-gated EditChild means the seed is as old as the open form. (d) I checked the ledger before filing: BUG-222 and BUG-273 name only apps/web files in their fixes, BUG-181's record says "Web and mobile screens for all of it" without any per-field claim, and no row records the mobile wholesale write as accepted-open. (e) I checked that the reverse direction is not already covered by something else: the mobile screen has no drift notice and no touched tracking at all (grep for seed/touched in children.tsx returns nothing).
findings.reproduction: No mobile test asserts this today, which is itself the gap. apps/mobile's vitest project cannot render react-native components (recorded in BUG-336's residual), so the honest reproduction is to move the body-building into a pure helper in apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.ts — e.g. `childEditBody(seed, fields, touched)` — and add to apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.test.ts the web case ported: with only the nickname edited, `expect(childEditBody(...)).toEqual({ nickname: 'Riley R.' })`. That is red today because no such helper exists and children.tsx:374 builds the body inline with all three fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the phone form the same rule the web form now has: a per-field `touched` flag set from each onChangeText/onChange, a body built from the touched fields only, and Save disabled until something is edited — with the body-building in a pure helper in apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.ts so it can be tested where react-native cannot be rendered. Do not reseed the fields from the live prop (that is HUNT5-F-1). While in the file, the archive button label at children.tsx:328 is unconditionally "Archive (keeps history, frees the slot)" and is rendered for a draft child that holds no slot — the WEBR4-12 branch the web card has at ChildrenPage.tsx:461-463 and mobile never got.

findings.title: `pairingRedeemable`'s comment claims "exactly the window in which the code works"; a consent withdrawal retires the code and leaves the child active, so the card keeps showing a code the tablet is refused
findings.claim_under_review: "Whether a pairing code this card is holding could still be redeemed. The redeem claim matches `c.status = 'active'` (apps/api/src/routes/child-auth.ts) and archiving does not consume an unexpired code, so \"active and not being deleted\" is exactly the window in which the code works." (ChildrenPage.tsx:227-231)
findings.mechanism: The redeem claim at apps/api/src/routes/child-auth.ts:128-138 requires FOUR things besides the code: `p.consumed_at is null`, `p.expires_at > now`, `c.status = 'active'` and `f.deleted_at is null`; and /pair then refuses separately when `consentAllowsChildAccess` is false (child-auth.ts:140-147, CS-R1-01). `pairingRedeemable` (ChildrenPage.tsx:232) establishes only the third and (indirectly) the fourth. Two of the missing conditions move without the child's status moving, so the card keeps a live-looking panel over a dead code. (1) POST /v1/consent/withdraw sets `consumed_at` on EVERY live code for the family (apps/api/src/routes/guardians.ts:729-731) and revokes sessions and devices, and does not touch child_profiles.status — so the child stays 'active', `pairingRedeemable` stays true, the panel keeps printing the code with "Enter this code. It works once" (ChildrenPage.tsx:769), and the tablet gets "That code did not work. Ask a grown-up for a new one." (child-auth.ts:107). Reachable with one action by the other guardian on their own device, and needing no race. (2) A provider-side consent flip with no route call at all leaves the code UNCONSUMED and the child active and /pair answers 422 CONSENT_REQUIRED — proved directly by apps/api/tests/consent-withdrawal.review.test.ts:168-185, which flips consent_records by SQL, pairs, gets CONSENT_REQUIRED, and asserts `consumed_at` is still null. (3) Minting a code for the same child on the phone consumes this one (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:444) while the status is unchanged.
findings.impact: A parent presses Create pairing code, walks to the child's tablet, and the code is refused — after the portal took a deliberate step in this round to remove codes that cannot work, and told the parent in its own comment that the remaining window is exactly the working one. The parent's recovery (press Create pairing code again) then answers CONSENT_REQUIRED honestly, so the trip to the tablet is the whole loss; but on the most common path (the other guardian withdrew consent) the card is showing a code the server has already retired.
findings.ruled_out: (a) I checked whether the page could know: it never reads /v1/consent (ChildrenPage.tsx has one query, GET /v1/family at :110), so the guard as written cannot be complete — which is why the comment's "exactly" is the thing to change first, not the code. (b) I checked whether the archive path already covers the consent case: it does not — POST /v1/consent/withdraw leaves status 'active', so `pairingRedeemable` is true and the new effect at :249 never fires. (c) I checked whether the PairingCodePanel's own copy already warns the parent: step 3 at :770 says "Creating a new code cancels this one", which covers case (3) if the parent connects the phone's code to this one, and says nothing about consent. (d) I checked whether the refusal is at least honest at the device: it is (child-safe wording, asserted in consent-withdrawal.review.test.ts:182), so this is a wasted trip rather than a misleading device message. (e) I checked whether removing a guardian could produce the same state for a still-mounted reader: guardians.ts:469-472 retires only the removed guardian's codes, and that guardian's next GET /v1/family is NOT_FOUND, so the card is replaced by an ErrorState — not the same case, and I am not claiming it.
findings.reproduction: The server side is already red-proven: apps/api/tests/consent-withdrawal.review.test.ts:168-185 shows an ACTIVE child's UNCONSUMED code refused by /pair. On this page, add a case to ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx's `[G-PROSE]` describe: mint a code for an active Riley, leave the status 'active' across a reload, and assert the card does not still present the code as usable — red today, and un-writable without the page learning the consent state, which is the point of the finding.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide which of the two is true (L-053) and say it: rewrite the comment to state what the guard establishes — a NECESSARY condition the page can observe, namely that a profile that is not active cannot redeem a code — and list the conditions it cannot see (the code retired by a consent withdrawal or by a code minted on another surface, a provider-side consent flip), with apps/api/tests/consent-withdrawal.review.test.ts:168-185 as the citation. Also soften the stale notice's "A code is only redeemed for a profile that is active" (:540-541), which states the same biconditional. If the product wants the guard to be complete, the Children page needs a /v1/consent read of its own, which is a larger change and should be a separate decision; do not weaken the server's consent gate for it.

findings.title: The portal-wide deletion-notice sweep detects only the literal phrase "you asked", and its anti-vacuity floor counts a status-label string literal as one of the "three notices"
findings.claim_under_review: The case name "holds for every deletion notice in the portal source, so a fourth cannot slip in" (:419) and the inline comment "Not vacuous: the three notices (plus the pickers' status label) are really being read." (:436)
findings.mechanism:
The scan is keyed on two literals. `NOTICE_MARKER = 'Data deletion under way'` (:403) is the only way a block is found, and `/\byou asked\b/i` (:432, and :443 for the wider pass) is the only way an offender is recognised. A fourth notice that leads with any other words is never scanned at all, and one that says "you requested", "you've asked", "at your request" or "your deletion request" passes both cases — the wider pass at :440-450 has exactly the same phrase dependency, only a broader window. Separately, the `notices >= 3` floor at :437 counts occurrences of the marker, not notices: in the current tree the marker appears five times (ChildrenPage.tsx:98 — a `return 'Data deletion under way';` inside childStatusLabel, not a notice; ChildrenPage.tsx:371; HomeworkPage.tsx:526 — an aria-label; HomeworkPage.tsx:528; LearningPlannerPage.tsx:122), so two of the three real notice paragraphs could be deleted and the floor would still be met by the label, the aria-label and one notice. For the label occurrence the block is not a notice at all: `text.indexOf('

', at)` from ChildrenPage.tsx:98 runs to the deletion notice's closing tag ~270 lines later and is truncated by the 900-character cap, so the block is arbitrary code and comments.
findings.impact: No user harm today (the three notices are currently correct). The cost is that the guard the round built to stop the fourth copy — after paying for this class of defect in BUG-290, BUG-291 and HUNT6-I-3 — is narrower than its own name, and its non-vacuity check cannot detect the notices going missing. L-057 is explicit that "the third copy is always somewhere"; a guard keyed on one phrase and one lead sentence is the kind that reports green while the fourth copy exists.
findings.ruled_out: (a) I checked that the test does go red for the defect it was written for: reverting the planner notice to "You asked for {name}'s data to be deleted" makes both :432 and :443 fire, so this is a narrow guard, not a dead one. (b) I checked whether another test covers the general property: grep for the phrase across apps/web finds only these two cases plus the per-page assertions at ChildrenPage.profile.test.tsx:216, ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx:675 and ArchivedChildCopy.test.tsx:411, all of which use the same `\byou asked\b` literal. (c) I checked the marker count by hand rather than assuming: `grep -c 'Data deletion under way'` over the non-test portal sources gives ChildrenPage 2, HomeworkPage 2, LearningPlannerPage 1. (d) I verified the label occurrence does not accidentally produce a false positive today (no "you asked" within its 900-character block), so the inflated count is the only consequence.
findings.reproduction: Change ChildrenPage.tsx:375 from "if you did not mean it" to "you requested this deletion, and if you did not mean it": both cases in `[G-THIRD-NOTICE]` stay green, and so do all the per-page assertions. Separately, delete the notice paragraphs at HomeworkPage.tsx:528 and LearningPlannerPage.tsx:122 and the `notices >= 3` floor still passes on the label, the aria-label and the remaining notice.
findings.suggested_fix: Key the sweep on the structure rather than one phrase: find each block by the `className="notice"` / `aria-label` node whose copy mentions a deletion, and reject any second-person attribution of the request to the reader — a set of patterns (asked, requested, your request, you chose) asserted over that set rather than the one phrase the last defect used (L-057: assert over a representative SET, not the names you fixed). Count real notice paragraphs for the non-vacuity floor, excluding the childStatusLabel string literal and the aria-label, and pin the expected count exactly so a deleted notice fails.

findings.title: The new effect turns a code already in hand stale but cannot touch one that arrives after the status change, so the panel the fix exists to close can still open on an archived child
findings.claim_under_review: "The pairing-code panel had no condition at all, so a code minted before the reload stayed on screen for a child who can no longer redeem it; the parent would have typed it into the device and been refused." and "one status change closes every open panel on this card" (ChildrenPage.tsx:234-243, 475-484)
findings.mechanism: The effect at ChildrenPage.tsx:244-250 is keyed on `[readOnly, pairingRedeemable]` and reads `code` only through a functional updater, so it acts exactly once per status change and only on whatever `code` holds at that moment. `createCode` (:274-286) sets `code` when its POST resolves, which can be after the status change: render N has the child active; the parent presses Create pairing code and the POST is in flight; a reload started by a sibling component — AddChildForm and each other card own their own useAction, so their buttons are live while this card's `busy` is 'code' — lands `archived` or `deletionPending: true`; the effect runs with `code === null` and does nothing; then the POST resolves and `setCode(result)` puts a real code panel on a card that is simultaneously rendering "nothing can be changed, paired or activated for them" (:370-376) or the archived branch. The effect does not re-run, because its deps have already settled.
findings.impact: The parent reads a freshly minted code, walks to the tablet and is refused — the precise outcome the round-6 comment says the fix removed. Needs three coincidences (an in-flight pairing POST, a second concurrent action on the page to trigger the reload, and a status change from the other guardian), so a parent reaches it rarely; the defect is that the guard's stated invariant is unconditional while the guard is not.
findings.ruled_out: (a) I checked whether this card's own buttons could produce the overlap, which would make it common: they cannot — every control on the card is `disabled={busy !== null}` (:382, :398, :444, :453, :501, :509) and `busy` is per-card. (b) I checked whether the reload can arrive without a second parent action: there is no polling and no auto-refresh; `onChanged` is called only from an action's success path, so a second action is genuinely required — which is why I am filing this low rather than medium. (c) I checked whether the server would refuse the mint and make the point moot: it would not — the parent presses the button while the child is still active, so POST /v1/children/:childId/pairing-code passes its `child.status !== 'active'` check (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:410-417) and returns a real code that the later archive then leaves unredeemable (archiving does not consume it; only the redeem claim's `c.status = 'active'` blocks it). (d) I checked the existing G-PROSE case: ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx:600-618 mints the code and awaits it BEFORE flipping the served status, so it exercises only the already-in-hand direction.
findings.reproduction: Add a case to the `[G-PROSE]` describe in ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx using a servingApi whose `/pairing-code` send returns a promise the test resolves manually: click Create pairing code, flip `serving.current` to the archived+deletionPending overview, run `addAChild`, wait for the deletion notice, THEN resolve the pairing promise, and assert `expect(within(await card('Riley')).queryByText('ABCD-EFGH')).toBeNull()`. Red today.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the rule hold at the point the code is stored rather than only at the status change: in `createCode`, set `'stale'` instead of the result when the child is no longer redeemable at resolve time, or derive the panel's state at render (`code !== null && !pairingRedeemable` renders the stale notice) so no ordering can put a live code on a non-redeemable card. Then correct the comment at :234-243 to describe the rule that actually holds.

findings.title: The Children page still tells a family whose plan lapsed they have "no paid child slots yet" — the exact word this diff removed from the planner, in the file the planner's fix named as its model
findings.claim_under_review: "Why activation is not on offer, for a draft and for an archived child alike: this portal never sells capacity, so the only honest answer is where a slot comes from (WEB-R1-04)." (ChildrenPage.tsx:188-191), over copy that reads "Your family has no paid child slots yet." (:194)
findings.mechanism: `noFreeSlotText` (ChildrenPage.tsx:192-196) returns "Your family has no paid child slots **yet**. To activate {nickname}, subscribe in the PencilLift app." whenever `paidSlots === 0`, and it is printed on the draft branch (:406) and the archived branch (:433). `releaseSlotlessProfiles` (apps/api/src/services/billing-sync.ts:1314-1324) sets `status = 'draft'` on a previously ACTIVE child whenever the verified provider state releases its slot (release_reason 'expired' or 'downgrade'), and family_capacity.paid_slots is then 0 for a family that has been paying. That population lands on this exact sentence for every one of their children, and "yet" asserts they never had a slot. This is HUNT6-H-4 verbatim: the same diff removed "yet" from the planner's draft branch and replaced it with "doesn't have a paid slot right now" (LearningPlannerPage.tsx:189-195), with a comment at :160-171 spelling out why "yet" is false for a lapsed plan and citing HomeworkPage's settled wording — and HUNT6-H-4's own suggested fix pointed at the Children page as the model for naming both remedies, without anyone grepping the Children page for the word being removed (L-057: "grep the repo for the sentence you just corrected").
findings.impact: A family whose subscription lapsed or was downgraded opens the page where they manage their children and is told, once per child, that they have never had a paid slot — while the copy the same product ships one click away says "doesn't have a paid slot right now" and "for example after the plan changed to fewer children". It is the one sentence that tells them what happened to the children they were paying for, and it says the wrong thing.
findings.ruled_out: (a) I checked that the population is real and not hypothetical: releaseSlotlessProfiles only moves `status = 'active'` children whose last slot release_reason is 'expired' or 'downgrade', so a previously active child really does arrive as a draft in a family whose paidSlots can be 0. (b) I checked whether the remedy named is at least right, so as not to overstate: it is — new capacity is bought in the app (WEB-R1-04), so only "yet" is false, which is why this is low. (c) I checked whether the round-6 diff touched this helper: `git diff b802686 5ba16c3 -- ChildrenPage.tsx` shows noFreeSlotText unchanged, so it is code the fix depended on rather than code the fix broke. (d) I checked whether a test pins the wrong wording: no case in ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx, ChildrenPage.profile.test.tsx or ArchivedChildCopy.test.tsx asserts this string; ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx:155 asserts only /in use/i on the other branch. (e) I checked the archived branch for a stronger claim before making one: a draft child can also be archived (WEBR4-12), so I am not claiming the card can prove the family once held a slot — the lapsed-plan population is the reachable case.
findings.reproduction: Add a case to ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx: `overview([{ id: RILEY, nickname: 'Riley', gradeLevel: 3, ageBand: '8-10', status: 'draft' }], 0)` and assert `expect((await card('Riley')).textContent).not.toMatch(/no paid child slots yet/i)` — red today. The mirror assertion already exists for the planner at ArchivedChildCopy.test.tsx:372-373.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the sentence state-neutral in the words the product has already settled on: "Your family has no paid child slots right now. To activate {nickname}, choose or renew a plan in the PencilLift app." Keep the other branch as it is. Then apply the same check to the mobile twin, `draftActivationNote` (apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.ts:113-119), which carries the identical "no paid child slots yet".

properties_attacked_and_held.property: HUNT6-G-8: an untouched field is never sent, so a save from one form cannot revert the other guardian's value in a field the parent did not edit.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Traced every writer of `touched` in both forms (ChildrenPage.tsx:679, :694, :709; FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:264, :277) looking for one outside a user onChange; checked whether `changes()` can leak an untouched key (spread is guarded per flag in both files); checked whether `nothingEdited` and the request body can disagree (both call the same `changes()`, so they cannot); checked whether the nickname/zone length validation, which runs on the UNTOUCHED seeded value, can inject a field (it cannot — it only returns early); checked whether `seed` still feeds the body anywhere (it does not, only `drifted`); checked whether a `<select>` can fire onChange without a user selection; checked whether reopening a form and pressing Save can send anything (touched resets on remount and Save is disabled).
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: `touched` is written only from the field onChange handlers, `changes()` adds a key only when its flag is true, `submit` returns before sending an empty body, and updateChildProfileRequestSchema / updateFamilyRequestSchema reject an empty body anyway (packages/contracts/src/family.ts). I could not construct a save that carries a field the parent never touched. The deliberate consequence — a field touched and returned to its seed value IS sent, and so overwrites a concurrent change — is stated in the code (FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:199-200) and warned about on screen, so it is a chosen trade-off, not a defect; my objection to that notice is only about the actor it names (HUNT7-G-2).

properties_attacked_and_held.property: G-PROSE: one status change closes every open panel on the Children card, and none of them reopens when the status changes back.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Walked active -> archived -> active and active -> deletionPending through the render order and the effect at ChildrenPage.tsx:244-250; checked the dep array for a stale closure over `code`; checked whether `confirmArchive` and `editing` are merely hidden by the render conditions at :472/:485 (they are also cleared); checked the reopen direction (the `if (readOnly)` branch is skipped on the way back); checked the mount run for a child who starts archived; checked whether a code already in hand survives (it becomes 'stale').
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: For state the card is already holding, the effect both hides and clears, and nothing reopens on the return path — the round-6 addition of the clear (not just the render condition) is what makes the claim true, and the test at ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx:620-646 goes red if the clear is reverted. findings.title: The schedule preview tells the parent of an archived or draft child "Today's daily practice is available." — three of the four daily-state strings carry no instant, so the notice's "the times below" framing cannot reach them
findings.claim_under_review: ScheduleSection.tsx:38-41: "HUNT5-F-10: the RELEASE TIMES do not branch on the status. For an archived profile the planner's own notice frames every time below it — 'the times below are what the schedule would produce if the profile were active again' — so these instants are read as the hypothetical they are"; and the production notice itself at LearningPlannerPage.tsx:180-189 ("no new practice is prepared for them … the times below are what the schedule would produce if the profile were active again") and :191-196 ("no practice is prepared, and the times below are what the schedule would produce while they hold one").
findings.mechanism: UpcomingReleases prints the daily line as `DAILY_STATE[data.dailyPractice.state](data.dailyPractice.releaseAt, zone)` (apps/web/src/components/learning/ScheduleSection.tsx:382). Only ONE of the four DAILY_STATE entries contains an instant: `not_yet_released` → "Today's daily practice opens <time>." (format.ts:115-116). The other three carry no time at all — `available` → "Today's daily practice is available." (format.ts:114), `paused` → "Daily practice is paused today." (:117), `vacation` → "Daily practice is paused today (vacation)." (:118) — so the notice's framing sentence, which speaks about "the times below", cannot frame them. `available` is reachable for both non-active statuses and is false in both: for an archived child GET /v1/children/:id/learning-schedule takes the `if (owned.archived)` branch (apps/api/src/routes/learning.ts:688-693) and computes dailyPractice from the stored plan plus the clock (scheduleResponse → dailyPracticeState, learning.ts:521-536), and `dailyPracticeState` returns reason 'available' on every local day once `daily_local_time` (default 15:30) has passed and no pause covers the day (packages/domain/src/scheduling/daily.ts:108-114); for a draft child the other branch (learning.ts:696-699, parentContext with requireActive:false) reaches the same computation. Nothing is in fact available to either: practice sets are only produced for an active profile — loadChildContext returns null for 'archived' and, with requireActive defaulting to true, for 'draft' (apps/api/src/jobs/learning-jobs.ts:224-225) — and no request from the child's device can open a set at all, because `app.current_child_id()` requires `c.status = 'active'` (supabase/migrations/0001_core_identity.sql:365). So, a few inches under a notice that says "no new practice is prepared for them", the same region asserts that today's daily practice is available.
findings.impact: A parent who archived a child to free a paid slot, or whose plan lapsed or was downgraded so the child is back to 'draft' (releaseSlotlessProfiles, apps/api/src/services/billing-sync.ts), opens the planner in the afternoon or evening and reads two opposite statements about the same child on one screen: no new practice is prepared, and today's daily practice is available. They cannot tell whether their child is still being given practice after the slot was released — the same confusion BUG-282 was filed for, in a sentence that fix's framing does not cover. The identical string is on the phone (apps/mobile/src/learning/planner-form.ts:204-209) under a notice that says "Everything below is what was planned" (apps/mobile/app/(parent)/planner.tsx:153-157), and there a DRAFT child gets no notice at all, so the claim stands unframed.
findings.ruled_out: (a) BUG-070's recorded residual (docs/Bug_Ledger.md:77) names only "Archived schedule preview still lists future releases" — that is the per-subject release instants, not a present-tense availability claim that contains no release instant, so this is not the deferred item; (b) BUG-282's fix, which this round extended, is explicitly about "the times below", and I checked each of the four strings: three have no time in them; (c) it is not merely unframed but false — I traced set generation (learning-jobs.ts:224-225) and the child's own read path (migration 0001:365) and neither can produce or open a set for a non-active profile; (d) not a stale-fixture artefact: the archived branch recomputes the state from `deps.clock()` on every request, so 'available' is the normal evening value, not an edge case; (e) the status is already in this component after round 6 (`childStatus`, ScheduleSection.tsx:58 and :96), so the fix needs no new plumbing on the web side and cannot be dismissed as "the section has no status"; (f) no test pins the sentence on either surface — grep shows only /daily practice opens/ asserted (ArchivedChildSections.test.tsx:140 and :155) and planner-form.test.ts:138 asserts only the paused line — so changing it weakens nothing; (g) this is not confined to one surface (L-037): the mobile twin builds the same string in buildUpcomingView.
findings.reproduction: apps/web/src/components/learning/ArchivedChildSections.test.tsx: change `SCHEDULE.dailyPractice.state` to 'available' and add to the existing case 'ScheduleSection: no "Save schedule" submit, and the saved schedule still readable' (which already renders with childStatus="archived") `expect((await screen.findByRole('region', { name: /coming up for riley/i })).textContent).not.toMatch(/daily practice is available/i)` — red today. Page level: make the same one-word change to `scheduleWithReleases.dailyPractice.state` in apps/web/src/pages/app/ArchivedChildCopy.test.tsx and assert it inside the /learning plan for riley/ region for both the archived family and the draft family.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the `childStatus` ScheduleSection already receives down into UpcomingReleases and, when it is not 'active', render the daily line as the conditional the set card already uses — keep the instant, drop the present-tense claim ("Daily practice would open for {name} at <time> once the profile is active[ again]"; for the paused and vacation states, "…would be paused today…"). That means DAILY_STATE needs a hypothetical variant per state rather than one string per state, so no state can print an unconditional present-tense sentence. Make the same change in apps/mobile/src/learning/planner-form.ts (buildUpcomingView takes the status) and its caller, and give the mobile draft case a notice or a conditional too.

findings.title: ArchivedChildSections.test.tsx's file docstring still states the round-5 design as current: "ScheduleSection therefore has no status to branch on at all" and "a draft really is waiting for a paid slot" — both contradicted by the same commit, one of them by a comment 170 lines below

findings.mechanism: Round 6 re-added the prop and the branch: ScheduleSection takes `childStatus?: string` (ScheduleSection.tsx:58), computes `readOnly={childStatus === 'archived'}` (:96) and branches on it in eight fields plus the submit and `submit()` itself (:170, :202-322, :351-363); the planner, its only caller, passes `child.status` (LearningPlannerPage.tsx:229). The same commit deleted the `@ts-expect-error -- ScheduleSection takes no childStatus prop` that used to enforce the docstring's first sentence, and added an inline comment at test line 125-127 saying "the prop is back, and it is wired" — but the file-level docstring above it still says the opposite, with the reason attached. The second claim is the premise HUNT6-H-4 established as false and removed everywhere else: `releaseSlotlessProfiles` (apps/api/src/services/billing-sync.ts) puts a previously ACTIVE child back into 'draft' when an expiry or store-confirmed downgrade releases its slot, which is why LearningPlannerPage.tsx:164-172 now records that "a draft really is waiting for a slot" was false and why this same test file's inline comment at :201-207 says so in full. Both stale sentences sit in the block a reader consults to learn what the file pins, and the first is the exact sentence the round-6 hunt cited as evidence (b) that no learning section branches on status — stale prose of this kind is how HUNT6-H-1 shipped in the first place.
findings.impact: The next reader of the file that pins the archived planner is told the schedule section has no status to branch on and that a draft child has never had a paid slot. The first would make them delete the prop the round-6 fix depends on (or trust that the schedule editor cannot be read-only); the second would re-introduce the "doesn't have a paid slot yet" wording HUNT6-H-4 removed. L-053: code and prose disagree here, and the code is right in both cases.
findings.ruled_out: (a) I checked the docstring is not scoped to history: it is written in the present tense about the shipped design ("therefore has no status to branch on at all … and is gone"), unlike the ledger rows, which are dated records; (b) I verified the prop is not vestigial — `readOnly` reaches eight controls and the submit early-return, and the planner really passes it, so the sentence is false rather than merely dated; (c) I checked that the round-6 commit did update the sibling comments (test line 125-127 and :201-207, plus the ScheduleSection and LearningPlannerPage docstrings), so this is an incomplete update rather than a deliberate wording choice; (d) I grepped the whole tree for the other copies of the claim ("takes no child status", "no status to branch", "never passed a status") and this test file is the only live source that still carries it — the hit in docs/hardening/round6-hunt-findings.json is a dated hunt record and is correct about b802686.
findings.reproduction: No assertion goes red — that is part of the defect: nothing in the suite reads the docstring, so both sentences can drift indefinitely. The check is to read ArchivedChildSections.test.tsx:27-29 against ScheduleSection.tsx:58/96/170 and LearningPlannerPage.tsx:229, and :38-39 against the same file's own comment at :201-207.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the two sentences to what the tree does: ScheduleSection takes the status and uses it for the EDITOR only (the release times stay whatever the status), and a 'draft' profile is either one that never held a paid slot or one a downgrade/expiry released, which is why no copy in the file says "again" for it. Keep the rest of the docstring, which is still accurate.

(:145-149). `matchedSkills` is computed from `scope_notes` by `toTestDate` regardless of status (apps/api/src/routes/learning.ts:735-755) and GET /test-dates admits an archived profile via `ownedChild(c, 'read')` (:760), so an archived child with a future test date and scope notes gets these sentences. findings.title: The schedule section tells the parent of an archived child to "Turn on at least one subject to get a review" while the subjects section, disabled by this same round's fix, says subjects can't be turned on or off
findings.claim_under_review: SubjectsSection.tsx:101-107 (new this round): "{childName}'s profile is archived, so subjects can't be turned on or off and no new subject can be added." versus ScheduleSection.tsx:384 on the same page: "No weekly reviews are scheduled yet. Turn on at least one subject to get a review."
findings.mechanism: `nextReviewReleases` is empty exactly when the child has no ENABLED bank subject: for an archived profile `storedPlan` builds the subject set as `BANK_SUBJECTS.filter(enabled.has(...))` from `child_subjects … and enabled` (apps/api/src/routes/learning.ts:472-486) and `scheduleResponse` drops non-bank subjects (:513), so an archived child whose subjects are all off — or one whose defaults were never created, because the subjects GET skips `ensureLearningDefaults` for an archived profile (learning.ts:626) — gets `nextReviewReleases: []`. ScheduleSection then renders the instruction at :384. The control it names is the subject checkbox, which round 6 made permanently unusable for this status: `disabled={readOnly || busy !== null}` (SubjectsSection.tsx:118) with `readOnly = childStatus === 'archived'` (:49), and the add-subject form is not rendered at all (:135). findings.ruled_out: (a) I checked the precondition is reachable rather than theoretical: with any enabled bank subject `scheduleResponse` iterates the current AND next ISO week (learning.ts:492) so a future release always exists, which means the empty case is precisely 'no enabled bank subject' — a parent who turned subjects off before archiving, a child whose only subjects are custom, and a child archived before the planner was ever opened (defaults are created only for a non-archived read, learning.ts:626); (b) the adjacent read-only notice in ScheduleSection (:352-356) explains only the SCHEDULE ("this schedule can't be changed"), not subjects, so it does not cover the sentence; (c) this is not the same as BUG-070's residual, which is about releases being LISTED, not about advice; (d) the contradiction is new: before round 6 no section claimed subjects could not be toggled; (e) the mobile planner prints only "No weekly reviews are scheduled yet." with no instruction (apps/mobile/app/(parent)/planner.tsx:410-411), so the defect is web-only and mobile needs no change.

properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Checked each archived case for a mounted-marker await before its negative assertions and for at least one positive assertion on stored data: ScheduleSection awaits the 'coming up for riley' region then asserts the daily-questions input has value '5' and disabled true; TestDatesSection awaits `findByLabelText('Saved test dates')` and asserts /adding fractions/i; SubjectsSection awaits the 'Subjects' region and asserts 'Math', 'On' and the checkbox's disabled property; StudyMaterialSection awaits its region and asserts the notice text. At page level, ArchivedChildCopy.test.tsx:305-334 awaits both the schedule region and the saved-test-dates list, asserts the Subjects and study-material headings, then the five absent submits, every checkbox disabled, the stored value '5' and the notice sentence; the draft twin asserts the same controls present and every checkbox enabled.

The planner-level mutation named in the ledger (removing `childStatus={child.status}` from one section) turns the page case red while the component cases stay green, which is the right division of labour between the two files.

findings.title: The new "no new scan" blocker line ends by promising these pages will go through after activation, for the three outcomes where the pages themselves are the blocker
findings.claim_under_review: ARCHIVED_CHILD_NO_NEW_SCAN_COPY / INACTIVE_CHILD_NO_NEW_SCAN_COPY: "Activate the profile again on the Children page, while a paid slot is free, and these pages can go through then." — and the HomeworkPage comment at line 183: "the outcomes whose advice is 'get a new scan', with the advice taken off ... A non-active profile keeps the outcome sentence and gets a blocker line instead of the advice."
findings.mechanism: explainStatus composes `${trimmed} ${blocked}` (apps/web/src/pages/app/HomeworkPage.tsx:250 and :264). `trimmed` comes from OUTCOME_WITHOUT_NEW_SCAN_ADVICE (HomeworkPage.tsx:183-197), which deliberately strips the SECOND half of each FAILED_FINAL_COPY line — the half that says HOW: FORMAT_NEEDS_CONVERSION loses "Scan the pages again as JPEG or PNG photos", SCAN_TOO_MANY_QUESTIONS loses "Split it into two scans with fewer pages each", needs_rescan loses "ask NAME to scan again with a clearer picture". `blocked` is ARCHIVED_CHILD_NO_NEW_SCAN_COPY (packages/contracts/src/privacy.ts:339) or INACTIVE_CHILD_NO_NEW_SCAN_COPY (:361), and both end "...and these pages can go through then." So the composed sentence asserts that the profile is the ONLY remaining blocker. It is not: the row is terminal (needs_rescan and failed_final are not in any resume path — packages/contracts/src/homework.ts:149-172 offers only cancel for needs_rescan, and scan-process.ts has no path back from failed_final), the same PDF/HEIC file is still unreadable after activation (scan-process.ts:1360 throws FORMAT_NEEDS_CONVERSION on the file type alone), the same over-dense worksheet still truncates (scan-process.ts:1291-1297), and the same blurred photos are still blurred. A parent who activates the profile (or assigns a slot) and re-sends the same pages meets the identical failure, with the one instruction that would have worked now deleted from the screen.
findings.impact: The parent of an archived or slot-less child is told, in the same sentence, that reactivating the profile is sufficient for these pages to be processed. For an archived child that reactivation costs a paid slot (and the Children page's remedy when none is free is to add capacity), so the false promise sits next to a spend decision. After acting on it they re-send the pages, hit the same permanent failure, and the screen no longer tells them to convert the file, split the worksheet or retake the photo.
findings.ruled_out: (1) I checked whether any resume path could make the promise true: CANCELLABLE/FINALIZED/CORRECTABLE_ASSIGNMENT_STATUSES (packages/contracts/src/homework.ts:149-177) give no way to re-run a needs_rescan or failed_final assignment, and scan-process.ts only re-enters from queued/failed_retryable (enterExtracting, ~line 946). (2) I checked whether the cause is still on screen so the parent could infer the remedy — it is ("PencilLift can't read PDF or HEIC files yet", "more questions than one check can handle", "hard to read (blur, glare...)"), which is why I am filing the final clause and the dropped instruction rather than claiming the whole line is uninformative. (3) I checked the sibling line ARCHIVED_CHILD_SCAN_COPY (privacy.ts:301), used for the CHILD_ARCHIVED code: it correctly ends "to scan this worksheet once more", because for that code the photos were fine — so the product already distinguishes the two cases and only the two new NO_NEW_SCAN strings collapse them. (4) I confirmed the composed text really reaches the screen on both surfaces: the list row (HomeworkPage.tsx:588) and the detail panel (HomeworkPage.tsx:1436), and that the new tests assert only the presence of the blocker, never the truth of its final clause.
findings.reproduction: apps/web/src/pages/app/HomeworkPage.test.tsx, describe '[HUNT6-H-2] ...', case 'replaces the rescan advice with the profile as the blocker for an archived child'. Add to it: expect(within(scans).queryByText(/these pages can go through then/i)).toBeNull() for the FORMAT_NEEDS_CONVERSION, SCAN_TOO_MANY_QUESTIONS and needs_rescan rows, and expect(within(scans).getByText(/as JPEG or PNG/i)) plus expect(within(scans).getByText(/Split it into two scans/i)). All four assertions are red today.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the blocker line in two: keep one string that states the profile blocker and the Children-page action and STOPS there (no claim about these pages), and re-append each code's own remedy after it, so the parent reads "...Activate the profile again on the Children page, while a paid slot is free. Then scan the pages again as JPEG or PNG photos." Concretely: change ARCHIVED_CHILD_NO_NEW_SCAN_COPY and INACTIVE_CHILD_NO_NEW_SCAN_COPY (packages/contracts/src/privacy.ts:339, :361) to end at the Children-page clause, and give OUTCOME_WITHOUT_NEW_SCAN_ADVICE a second field per key holding the deferred remedy ("Then scan the pages again as JPEG or PNG photos.", "Then split it into two scans with fewer pages each.", "Then ask NAME to scan again with a clearer picture.", and nothing for failed_final/uploading), composed after `blocked` in explainStatus. Do not weaken the existing negative assertion on RESCAN_ADVICE: the deferred remedies are phrased as conditional next steps, so keep the regex and pin the new wording alongside it.

findings.title: AssignmentDetail was given the child's status "so the panel does not ask for a refused rescan" but still offers Fix transcription, which the API refuses for exactly those children
findings.claim_under_review: apps/web/src/pages/app/HomeworkPage.tsx:1387 — "/** HUNT6-H-2: the same status the list rows use, so the panel does not ask for a refused rescan. */ childStatus: string;"
findings.mechanism: AssignmentDetail now receives `childStatus` (HomeworkPage.tsx:1382, threaded in at :636) and uses it for the status label and explanation only (:1435-1437). The correction control is still gated on the assignment status alone: `correctable={CORRECTABLE_ASSIGNMENT_STATUSES.includes(query.data.assignment.status)}` (HomeworkPage.tsx:1466), and CORRECTABLE_ASSIGNMENT_STATUSES is ['ready','needs_parent_review'] (packages/contracts/src/homework.ts:175). QuestionCard therefore renders the "Fix transcription" button (HomeworkPage.tsx:1587-1595) for every finished scan of an archived or draft child. POST /v1/questions/:id/correction calls assertCanCollect (apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:1371), whose readPaidProfile requires `status === 'active'` plus an unreleased paid slot (:410-413), so the submit is refused with BUSINESS_RULE CHILD_NOT_ACTIVE and the message a non-active profile gets, 'Assign a paid slot to this child before scanning homework' (:446-451). That string is rendered verbatim by ActionFeedback -> ErrorState (HomeworkPage.tsx:390, :1624). The needs_parent_review row makes it worse: its explanation invites exactly this action ("Some answers need your review before NAME sees a final result. Open the scan to check them.", HomeworkPage.tsx:117-121) and is NOT trimmed for a non-active child, because OUTCOME_WITHOUT_NEW_SCAN_ADVICE has no 'needs_parent_review' key.
findings.impact: A parent who archives a child (one click from the Children page) or whose plan downgraded, opens an old finished scan, sees the transcription flagged "Transcription may be wrong — hard to read", presses Fix transcription, retypes the answer, saves — and is told to assign a paid slot before scanning homework, in reply to a correction. Nothing is saved and the wording does not name what they were actually doing. The same control on a needs_parent_review scan is the action the row's own copy asks for.
findings.ruled_out: (1) I checked the sibling control: POST /v1/questions/:id/override (apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:1273) does NOT call assertCanCollect, so "Change result" genuinely works for an archived child — the fix must gate only the correction, not the whole panel, and this is why I am not proposing to hide the panel. (2) I checked the cancel path (routes/homework.ts:1040-1090): no assertCanCollect, so "Cancel scan" is not a dead end. (3) I checked GET /v1/assignments/:id/solutions (:1222): no assertCanCollect, so "Show solutions" works. (4) I checked whether the refusal could damage state: assertCanCollect runs before the update inside the same asService transaction (:1371 before :1373), so the throw rolls back — no partial write. (5) I checked whether an existing or new test already covers it: every new panel case in this round uses `questions: []` (HomeworkPage.test.tsx, '[HUNT6-H-2] says it in the open scan's detail panel too' and '[G-H2] says it in the open scan's detail panel too'), so no test in the round ever renders a QuestionCard for a non-active child. (6) I confirmed the consent variant is pre-existing and not what I am filing: assertCanCollect also refuses on withdrawn consent for an ACTIVE child, which this change did not touch.
findings.reproduction: apps/web/src/pages/app/HomeworkPage.test.tsx: render HomeworkPage with ARCHIVED_FAMILY, a list of [summary(READY,'ready')], and `/v1/assignments/${READY}` -> detail() (the existing helper, which has two questions). Open the scan and assert expect(within(panel).queryByRole('button', { name: 'Fix transcription' })).toBeNull(). Red today — the button renders.
findings.suggested_fix:
Pass the child's status into the correctable decision: `correctable={childStatus === 'active' && CORRECTABLE_ASSIGNMENT_STATUSES.includes(query.data.assignment.status)}` and give QuestionCard a second reason string so the existing `{!correctable ?

Transcriptions can be fixed once checking has finished.

}` branch (HomeworkPage.tsx:1598) says the true reason for a non-active profile instead — e.g. a short line stating that a correction re-checks the work, which needs a paid slot, and naming the Children page, keyed the same way noNewScanCopy is. Keep 'Change result' available, because the override route allows it.

findings.title: The new [G-H2] test pins "start a new scan with clear photos" as the right answer for an active child's STAGE_LIMIT and AI_NOT_AVAILABLE scans, where the photos are not the cause and no new scan can succeed
findings.claim_under_review: apps/web/src/pages/app/HomeworkPage.test.tsx:1511 — it('keeps the generic advice for an ACTIVE child, where a new scan is the answer') asserting getAllByText(/Please start a new scan with clear photos/i) has length UNLISTED_FINAL_CODES.length, for a list that includes 'AI_NOT_AVAILABLE', 'STAGE_LIMIT', 'UNKNOWN_MODEL' and 'MODERATION_NOT_AVAILABLE'.
findings.mechanism: explainStatus falls through to STATUS_COPY[status].explain for any failed_final code with no line of its own (HomeworkPage.tsx:267), and STATUS_COPY.failed_final.explain is 'This scan could not be processed after several tries. Please start a new scan with clear photos.' (HomeworkPage.tsx:127-131). The round-6 change enumerates those codes in its own comment (HomeworkPage.tsx:170-179) and in UNLISTED_FINAL_CODES (test:1451-1466), routes them to the state line for a NON-active child, and then asserts the photo-blaming line as correct for an active child. Two of the enumerated codes cannot be cleared by any new scan: AI_NOT_AVAILABLE is thrown when checkChildDataGate refuses (apps/api/src/jobs/scan-process.ts:1145), i.e. the ZDR approval reference is missing, placeholder-like or dated in the future, or a mock provider is configured in production (packages/ai/src/gate.ts:54-72) — an operator-side state that refuses every subsequent scan for every child identically; STAGE_LIMIT is the pre-flight admission refusal for a request too large to admit, thrown with zero provider calls (packages/ai/src/routing.ts:71-78, converted to PermanentFailure at scan-process.ts:1280), whose real remedy is the SCAN_TOO_MANY_QUESTIONS one — split the worksheet — and which routing.ts's own comment already records as "a bare STAGE_LIMIT, which has no copy of its own". UNKNOWN_MODEL is router configuration. In all of these the photos were never read or were fine, and "several tries" is also false: STAGE_LIMIT and AI_NOT_AVAILABLE are single permanent refusals.
findings.impact: When the owner's ZDR evidence lapses, every parent in the product is told their child's homework photos were not clear enough and to scan again; each rescan fails the same gate at once. For a dense worksheet the parent is told the same thing forever, while the one action that works — splitting it — is never mentioned. This is the defect HUNT5-F-5 and HUNT6-H-2 were opened for (do not blame the photos for a cause that is not the photos), left standing for active children and now locked in by a test whose name asserts the opposite.
findings.ruled_out: (1) I checked that the affected codes are reachable: AI_NOT_AVAILABLE from gate.ts:54-72 via scan-process.ts:1145 (assertMayProcess runs on every initial scan), STAGE_LIMIT per the measured bounds in packages/ai/src/routing.ts:55-78 ("a worksheet of ten dense pages can still be cut off in grading with no retry"). (2) I checked whether the wrong copy costs the family pages, which would raise this to high: it does not — every PermanentFailure calls settleReservation('failed_final') (scan-process.ts:977-978) and the dead-letter path releases too (:839), so a futile rescan does not burn the monthly allowance. (3) I checked whether some of the listed codes DO deserve the generic line, so the fix must not be a blanket change: PROCESSING_ERROR and PROCESSING_TIMEOUT are a crash and a lost lock (scan-process.ts:816), NO_PAGES and SCAN_TOO_LARGE come from the pages themselves, and *_REQUEST_REJECTED includes "an image it cannot read" (:1282-1286) — a retry can help for those, so only the operator-side codes need their own line. (4) I checked that no other surface already says it honestly: the child app's failed_final copy is 'We couldn't read this one' (apps/mobile/src/homework/result-view.ts) and there is no parent homework screen in apps/mobile, so the portal is the only parent surface. (5) I confirmed the assertion is not merely incidental: it is the test's whole body and its title states the property.
findings.reproduction: apps/web/src/pages/app/HomeworkPage.test.tsx: with the default active `family`, a list of [{...summary(FINAL,'failed_final'), errorCode:'STAGE_LIMIT'}], assert expect(within(scans).queryByText(/with clear photos/i)).toBeNull() and expect(within(scans).getByText(/split/i)). Red today. The same for errorCode 'AI_NOT_AVAILABLE' with an assertion that the line does not ask for a new scan.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the operator-side permanent codes their own honest lines in FAILED_FINAL_COPY (HomeworkPage.tsx:142-164, wording in packages/contracts/src/privacy.ts beside the existing four): STAGE_LIMIT reuses the SCAN_TOO_MANY_QUESTIONS remedy (the worksheet is too big for one check — split it, pages given back); AI_NOT_AVAILABLE and UNKNOWN_MODEL say PencilLift could not check this scan, that nothing was wrong with the photos, that the pages were given back, and that PencilLift is fixing it — asking for nothing, since no parent action helps. Then split UNLISTED_FINAL_CODES in the test into the codes that keep the state line (PROCESSING_ERROR, PROCESSING_TIMEOUT, NO_PAGES, SCAN_TOO_LARGE, the *_REQUEST_REJECTED and *_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED codes, STORAGE_READ_FAILED, null) and the codes that must not blame the photos, and assert both lists positively. This strengthens the test rather than weakening it: the non-active-child assertions stay exactly as they are, since a code with its own line still goes through branch 1/2 of explainStatus.

findings.title: PrivacyControlsPage still cites AccountDeletionPage's removed SERVER_NOT_TOLD constant and claims it is word for word SignOutControl's, which the same commit made false
findings.claim_under_review: apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:786-788 — "The report now travels in the router state and /account-deletion says that sentence beside the closure notice (AccountDeletionPage's SERVER_NOT_TOLD, word for word SignOutControl's, which reports the same fact on its own path)."

No parent sees anything wrong.
findings.ruled_out: (1) I grepped SERVER_NOT_TOLD across apps/web/src: only SignOutControl.tsx:32 defines or uses it, so the citation cannot resolve. (2) I checked the other removal from the same edit, the `unverified` local, for a dangling reference: the only remaining mentions are the HUNT6-G-1 paragraph correctly describing it as the thing that was removed (:799) and an unrelated use of the word about co-guardian email verification (:1227) — clean. (3) I checked that the new two-string split is the intended behaviour and not itself the defect: packages/contracts/src/account.ts:66-101 and the lead's HUNT6-G-6 decision both state it, so the code is right and the prose is wrong (L-053). findings.reproduction: No runtime test can go red on a comment. The check is textual: `grep -n SERVER_NOT_TOLD apps/web/src/pages/public/AccountDeletionPage.tsx` returns nothing, while apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.test.tsx:1391 asserts notice.textContent contains SIGN_OUT_NOT_TOLD_COPY.signInClosed, which SignOutControl never says.

findings.title: The replace-instead-of-push fix is justified by a Back that cannot happen, and its test measures history depth in a one-entry router instead of portal reachability
findings.claim_under_review: apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:833-836 — "Replaced, not pushed: this page needs a signed-in parent and re-reads the session to render (RequireParent), and on the `pending` path that session is deliberately still valid until the family purge finishes — so one Back used to put the next person at a shared computer back inside the parent portal, on the account that was just closed (HUNT6-G-1)." And PrivacyControlsPage.test.tsx:1134, it('[HUNT6-G-1] leaves no history entry to go back into the portal with').
findings.mechanism: The navigation at :837-840 is reached only when the local session is gone: either `signOutRefused === false`, which the Supabase adapter returns only when auth.signOut resolved without error and therefore removed the stored session (apps/web/src/lib/supabase-auth.ts:430-433), or `signOutRefused === true` and `stillSignedIn()` answered false (:831). RequireParent does not read the server-side sign-in; it reads THIS browser's session, through useParentSession, whose state starts 'loading' and is refreshed by an effect on every mount (apps/web/src/lib/session.tsx:72-93, 117-130). A Back navigation remounts the route element, so the read runs again and returns null, and the page renders SignInPrompt. The comment's mechanism therefore requires a surviving local session, which this branch has just excluded — it conflates the server-side sign-in that `pending` keeps alive with the stored session RequireParent actually reads, the exact conflation HUNT6-G-1 corrected 30 lines above. Separately, `replace: true` removes only the /app/privacy entry; a real browser history also holds /app, /app/children and so on, so if the premise were true one more Back would re-enter the portal anyway. The test cannot see this because createMemoryRouter is built with initialEntries: ['/app/privacy'] (PrivacyControlsPage.test.tsx:45), so after a replace the history has a single entry and router.navigate(-1) is clamped to it — the assertion is about history depth, not about whether the portal renders.
findings.impact: No parent or child is harmed: the property the fix aims at holds for a different reason, and replace is harmless. The cost is to the next reader and to the records — a comment that states a shared-computer hole which the code refutes, and a regression test that would keep passing on an app whose history holds any other portal entry.
findings.ruled_out: (1) I checked for a navigating path where the session could survive: the success path does not re-read, but the adapter returns void only when auth-js's signOut resolved with no error, which removes the stored session; the unconfigured adapter (lib/auth.ts, unconfiguredAuth) cannot reach this code because RequireParent renders the 'not available' notice instead. (2) I checked that RequireParent really re-reads rather than trusting a cached shell state: useParentSession holds its own useState per consumer and each page wraps itself in its own RequireParent (HomeworkPage.tsx:64, PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:52, RewardsPage.tsx:42), so a remount always re-reads; the stale-shell problem SignOutControl describes (WEBR5-E-2) affects only the header line, which is not a gate. (3) I verified the test is not vacuous about the thing it does test: with push it would land on /app/privacy and fail, so it does pin replace — it simply does not pin reachability. (4) I did not conclude the change should be reverted: replace is the right call regardless.
findings.reproduction: apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.test.tsx:1134. Build the same router with initialEntries: ['/app', '/app/privacy'] instead of ['/app/privacy'] and keep the current assertions: after the closure and one router.navigate(-1) the location is '/app', not '/account-deletion', so the depth assertion fails while the real property (no portal content renders) still holds — which is the evidence that the test measures the wrong thing.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the comment to say what is true: the navigation replaces the portal entry so the closed account's page is not one Back away, and the protection that actually holds is RequireParent's re-read of this browser's session, which this branch has already verified is gone. Then make the test assert the property: give the memory router initialEntries ['/app', '/app/privacy'], add a route for '/app' behind RequireParent, and after Back assert that no portal content renders and the sign-in prompt does.

findings.title: The uploader region's unhedged "You can set that up on the Children page" is the only draft sentence on the Homework page the round did not hedge, and the new [G-DRAFT] test calls the two regions agreed
findings.claim_under_review: apps/web/src/pages/app/HomeworkPage.test.tsx:1554 — it('never says the profile had a paid slot before, and agrees with the uploader region'), whose only assertion about that region is getByText(/needs a paid child slot before homework can be scanned/).
findings.mechanism: This round hedged every draft-child remedy on the page because the portal cannot sell capacity (WEB-R1-04): INACTIVE_CHILD_SCAN_COPY and INACTIVE_CHILD_NO_NEW_SCAN_COPY both say "Assign one of your family's unused paid slots to this profile on the Children page, while one is free" (packages/contracts/src/privacy.ts:317, :361), and the new NoScans branch repeats it (HomeworkPage.tsx:1047-1050). uploadBlockedReason was left as "NAME needs a paid child slot before homework can be scanned. You can set that up on the Children page." (HomeworkPage.tsx:983-988). findings.ruled_out: (1) I confirmed both regions render together for a draft child: ChildHomework renders ScanUploader for every non-archived status (HomeworkPage.tsx:565) and the Scans card below it, and the new test itself reads both. (2) I confirmed the Children page does not silently buy capacity: childActivationResponseSchema's doc and NEEDS_PAID_SLOT (packages/contracts/src/family.ts:132-137) say it never purchases. (3) I checked that this is not merely duplicate wording I should ignore as style: the round's own decisions (HUNT6-H-4, G-DRAFT-COPY) treat the missing hedge as the defect, and the approved prices and the no-capacity-promise rule are project constraints. (4) I checked whether the archived branch has the same gap: it does not — uploadBlockedReason is never reached for an archived child (the notice at HomeworkPage.tsx:554 replaces the uploader), so only the draft sentence needs changing.
findings.reproduction: apps/web/src/pages/app/HomeworkPage.test.tsx:1554. Add expect(within(add).getByText(/while one is free/i)).toBeTruthy() — or assert that the Add-a-scan region's text matches the same remedy the Scans region prints. Red today.
findings.suggested_fix: Make uploadBlockedReason's non-active branch print the same hedged remedy the three sibling sentences use — "NAME needs a paid child slot before homework can be scanned. Assign one of your family's unused paid slots to this profile on the Children page, while one is free." — and extend the [G-DRAFT] assertion so the test's title is what it checks: both regions name the same blocker and the same hedged action.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: G-H2: no failed_final code can reach the generic "Please start a new scan with clear photos" line for a non-active child, without anyone having to add future codes to a table.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: I tried to find a key that walks past all three branches of explainStatus (HomeworkPage.tsx:239-268). I enumerated every PermanentFailure and exhausted-RetryableFailure code in apps/api/src/jobs/scan-process.ts (CHILD_ARCHIVED, CHILD_NOT_ACTIVE, CONSENT_REQUIRED, AI_NOT_AVAILABLE, NO_PAGES, FORMAT_NEEDS_CONVERSION, SCAN_TOO_LARGE, STAGE_LIMIT, UNKNOWN_MODEL, *_REQUEST_REJECTED, SCAN_TOO_MANY_QUESTIONS, *_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED, moderation codes, STORAGE_READ_FAILED, PROCESSING_ERROR, PROCESSING_TIMEOUT, null) and checked each against the two tables; I also looked for a status/code key collision in the single flat Record that serves both (a code literally equal to 'uploading', 'needs_rescan' or 'failed_final') and for an inherited Object.prototype key reaching the lookup.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: Branch 3 keys on the assignment STATE, and 'failed_final' is in the table, so every unlisted or null code is answered by the state line. Error codes are SCREAMING_SNAKE and statuses lowercase, so the double duty of the one table cannot collide; and errorCode comes only from the API's own vocabulary, so no prototype key is reachable. The property holds for non-active children — it is the ACTIVE child, where the generic line survives on purpose, that HUNT7-I-3 is about.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: G-LABEL: the row header and detail prefix never ask a non-active child's parent for a new scan, and every other status label is a description rather than an imperative the profile can refuse.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: I read all thirteen labels in STATUS_COPY (HomeworkPage.tsx:95-137) looking for a second imperative the API refuses for an archived or draft child, and checked the control each one implies against the routes: 'Needs your review' against POST /v1/questions/:id/override, the cancellable statuses against POST /v1/assignments/:id/cancel, and 'Uploading' against the uploads/finalize routes. I also checked that the new label reaches both surfaces and that nothing else in the tree matches on the old label string.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: Only needs_rescan's label is an imperative for a refused action. Override (routes/homework.ts:1273) and cancel (:1040) carry no assertCanCollect, so 'Needs your review' and the Cancel button are honest for an archived child; the uploading label's advice was separately trimmed. statusLabel is called from both the row (:588) and the panel (:1435), and grep shows no other consumer of 'Needs a new scan'. The neighbouring control that IS refused is Fix transcription, which is a button rather than a label — filed as HUNT7-I-2.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: G-I3-WEB: the portal's homework deletion notice names the open request rather than the reader, and a co-guardian is never told they asked for a deletion.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: I checked whether the flag the notice branches on can carry a requester, and whether the notice can be shown to the wrong adult or bypassed: I read the deletionPending computation in apps/api/src/routes/family.ts (:136-147, :243), the optional field in familyChildSchema (packages/contracts/src/family.ts:66-79) and the page's own local z.object (HomeworkPage.tsx:82-90), and looked for a path where the early return at HomeworkPage.tsx:521 is skipped while assignments still render.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: GET /v1/family always emits deletionPending and never emits requested_by, so no sentence can attribute the request; the local schema names the field, so it is not stripped (the HUNT5-F-2 failure mode); and the early return sits above every query-state branch, so a deletion-pending child can never reach the rows, the uploader or the NoScans copy.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: HUNT6-G-1: the public deletion page's "This computer is signed out" is only ever printed after the closure flow has read the session and found it gone.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: I tried to reach AccountDeletionPage's refusal notice with a live local session. I traced every exit of the submit handler in AccountCloseSection (PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:750-841), the adapter's two report shapes (apps/web/src/lib/supabase-auth.ts:396-434), the throw path, a currentSession() that throws (stillSignedIn returns true), and the success path that does not re-read; I also checked that signOutRefused cannot be forged from a URL (it is router state only, AccountDeletionPage.tsx:37-39) and that the notice is tied to an in-app closure (:68).
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: Both refusal paths now go through stillSignedIn(), and the only path that skips the read is the adapter's success, which auth-js reaches only after removing the stored session. A currentSession() that throws is treated as still signed in, so it keeps the parent on the portal. The sentence is licensed on every path that can print it.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: HUNT6-G-6: the closed-account remedy asks for nothing the deletion has made impossible, and the pending remedy names an action the parent can carry out.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: I checked that 'closed' really means the sign-in is gone before the page asserts "your sign-in is closed, so there is nothing left to do": I read POST /v1/account/close end to end (apps/api/src/routes/account.ts:30-110), including closeNow's try/catch and the owner branch, and checked that 'pending' is returned whenever the auth service could not be reached. I also searched the whole page for the retracted 'sign out on your phone' remedy that the test forbids with a body-wide negative.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: closeNow returns true only when authAdmin.closeUser resolved, and every other outcome answers 'pending' with a durable retry job, so the 'closed' string never over-claims. No copy on the public page matches /on your phone/, so the negative assertion is not passing by accident on a page that lacks the phrase for another reason — the page does mention phones, but as 'your iPhone, iPad, Android phone or tablet'.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: HUNT6-G-2 (RewardsPage): the points-balance row cannot say "history only" about history a purge is deleting.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: I verified the comment's three load-bearing claims rather than trusting them: that GET /v1/rewards filters the child list (apps/api/src/routes/rewards.ts:335-340 notBeingDeleted, applied at :394), that rewardChildBalanceSchema is a strictObject with no deletionPending (packages/contracts/src/rewards.ts:180-186) so no flag could be branched on, and that the childStatusLabel branch it points at exists (apps/web/src/pages/app/ChildrenPage.tsx:92-106). I then looked for a sibling row on the same page that could print the stale sentence from another source (recentRequests, openRequests, HistorySection).
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: Every child list in that response is filtered by notBeingDeleted, including the request lists, so no deletion-pending child reaches any row on the page and there is nothing to mislabel. Worth recording for the owner, not filed because the fix would need a contract change the comment itself defers: a family whose only child is under deletion now sees BalancesSection's empty state, "Points appear once a child is set up. Add a child to get started." (RewardsPage.tsx:381-384) — misleading, but unfixable in the page while the API omits the child entirely.

findings.title: The mobile family view still prints "Status: Archived: history only" for a child whose data deletion is under way — the sweep the lead's own HUNT6-G-2 decision ordered, in a file this round edited
findings.claim_under_review: docs/hardening/round6-fix-plan.json, lead_decisions.HUNT6-G-2: "CONFIRMED. One helper decides the sentence for every surface (L-037): give childStatusLabel the deletionPending branch, and sweep the other printers the finding names — RewardsPage and the mobile family view — in the same pass. A parent must never read 'history only' about history that is being deleted."
findings.mechanism: `childStatusText(status)` (apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.ts:54-63) takes ONLY the status and returns 'Archived: history only' for 'archived'. `childRows` calls it that way (family-view.ts:129) and carries no deletionPending signal at all — `grep -rn deletionPending apps/mobile/` matches only app/(parent)/children.tsx and two test files, never family-view.ts. Every deletion-pending child IS archived: `public.request_deletion` runs `update public.child_profiles set status = 'archived'` for a child-scope target (supabase/migrations/0890_hardening_r4_db.sql:89; migration 0600 line 68), and GET /v1/family returns that row with `status: 'archived'` and `deletionPending: true` (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:215-244). So both mobile printers of `row.statusText` render the false sentence: app/(parent)/children.tsx:224 renders `Status: {row.statusText}` immediately above the deletion notice at :225-265 that says the child's data is being deleted (the exact two-lines-apart contradiction HUNT6-G-2 filed for apps/web/src/pages/app/ChildrenPage.tsx:308), and app/(parent)/home.tsx:94 renders it with NO deletion notice anywhere on the screen, which is the same defect HUNT5-F-2 fixed on the web dashboard row. The web side of the sweep was done — apps/web/src/pages/app/ChildrenPage.tsx:92-99 now tests `child.deletionPending === true` first and both web callers pass the child object (ChildrenPage.tsx:355, FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:151) — and the RewardsPage leg was examined and documented (RewardsPage.tsx:401-412). The mobile leg was not, although apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.ts is in the R6-H-mobile file list and this commit added `loadStateForRun` and `childPlanEditable` to it.
findings.impact: A parent who has requested deletion of one child's data opens the mobile parent home and reads "Status: Archived: history only" for that child, with nothing on the screen saying a deletion is under way. "History only" says the history is KEPT; the purge enqueued with the request is deleting it. This is the state where the project's own copy elsewhere says "contact support straight away" because the purge cannot be undone from the app — a parent who mis-targeted the request and is reassured by this line spends the only window in which support could still stop it. On the Children screen the same line contradicts the notice printed two lines below it, so the parent cannot tell which statement to believe.
findings.ruled_out: 1) I checked whether `deletionPending` even reaches mobile: `familyChildSchema` carries it (packages/contracts/src/family.ts:66-80) and GET /v1/family always sets it, so the data is present and the omission is in the view model, not the payload. 2) I checked whether some other mobile code already corrects the label: children.tsx suppresses the pair/activate/edit/archive controls on `deletionPending` (children.tsx:267, 281, 291) but never touches `statusText`; home.tsx (line 89-96) renders nickname, detail and statusText and nothing else. 3) I checked whether a family-scope request could make this unreachable — it cannot substitute, because a family-scope request revokes every adult membership with the tombstone so currentFamilyId() answers NOT_FOUND and no child card renders at all; the reachable case is the child-scope request, which leaves every other membership active. 4) I checked the other `statusText` producer, `deviceRows` (family-view.ts:190-199), which prints only Connected/Disconnected and is not affected. 5) I confirmed the web fix is real and not merely planned, so this is a surface that was left behind rather than a finding already closed.
findings.suggested_fix: Give `childStatusText` the flag, exactly as apps/web/src/pages/app/ChildrenPage.tsx:92-99 does: take the child (or `{status, deletionPending}`) and return 'Data deletion under way' when `deletionPending === true`, before the status switch. Pass the child through from `childRows` (family-view.ts:129), which already has it. Add the deletion-pending case to family-view.test.ts (today's `family` fixture has no such child, so the suite passes vacuously on it) and a source pin in children-screen.test.ts that the home and Children rows cannot print /history only/ for a deletion-pending child.
findings.reproduction: apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.test.ts — add to the 'spells out child status' case a child `{...RILEY, status: 'archived', deletionPending: true}` and assert `childRows(...)[0].statusText` is 'Data deletion under way'. Today it is 'Archived: history only' and the assertion goes red.

findings.title: The mobile Practice planner has no deletion-pending branch: it calls an archived-and-being-purged child read-only "history", then shows "That child or subject was not found. Pull to refresh." twice on a screen with no pull-to-refresh
findings.claim_under_review: planner.tsx:135-136 — "The API refuses every learning write for an archived profile (HUNT6-H-1), so no control for one is offered: the stored plan stays readable, which is what archiving promises" — and family-view.ts:66-78, "Whether the parent may still change a child's practice plan … while the reads behind the same screen succeed".
findings.mechanism: `ownedChild` (apps/api/src/routes/learning.ts:195-211) excludes any child with a `requested`/`processing` deletion request from BOTH access modes and throws NOT_FOUND before the archived check, so GET /v1/children/:id/subjects (learning.ts:622) and GET /v1/children/:id/learning-schedule (learning.ts:686) both answer 404 for a deletion-pending child. GET /v1/family still lists that child (family.ts:215-244), so planner.tsx:80-90 puts it in `children`, and `childId = children.some(...) ? picked : (children[0]?.id ?? null)` selects it by default when it is first (the only choice for a one-child family). Because `request_deletion` sets `status = 'archived'` (migration 0890:89), `childPlanEditable(child.status)` (family-view.ts:76-78, called at planner.tsx:136) returns false, so the archived Notice at planner.tsx:152-159 renders: "{nickname} is archived, so their practice plan is read-only. Everything below is what was planned; make them active again in Children to change it." Nothing below it is: both `useLoad`s (planner.tsx:138-147) fail, so the two ErrorBoxes at :166-172 and :186-193 render `plannerError(...).message`, which for NOT_FOUND is 'That child or subject was not found. Pull to refresh.'
