(apps/mobile/src/learning/planner-form.ts:236-238) — and the planner renders inside `<Screen>` (src/family/ui.tsx:50-83), whose ScrollView has no RefreshControl, so there is no pull to refresh. The web planner has exactly the branch this screen lacks: apps/web/src/pages/app/LearningPlannerPage.tsx:103-131 returns a deletion notice and loads nothing, with the comment "a child whose data deletion is under way has no plan to show and no subjects to load (GET /v1/children/:id/subjects answers NOT_FOUND for it). Nothing here may promise that what was planned and practised stays readable, or offer an activation the API refuses" (HUNT5-F-2, round 5).
findings.impact: A parent who has asked for one child's data to be deleted opens the Practice planner for that child (automatically, if it is their only or first child) and is told the plan is kept and readable, told to "make them active again in Children" — an activation both the Children screen (children.tsx:281) and the API (`visibleChild` in family.ts) refuse for that child — and then told twice that the child "was not found", which is the misleading answer FL-R4-04 removed from PATCH /v1/children precisely because "a 404 there protected nothing and only claimed a profile the parent can still see does not exist" (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:222-227). The instruction it gives to recover — pull to refresh — is impossible on that screen.
findings.ruled_out: 1) I checked that `ownedChild` really refuses the READ and not only the write: the `not exists (… deletion_requests …)` predicate is in the shared query before `if (archived && access === 'write')` (learning.ts:200-210), so 'read' is refused too. 2) I checked whether the deletion-pending child could be absent from GET /v1/family (which would make it unreachable): it is deliberately kept, and the contract comment says so (packages/contracts/src/family.ts:72-79). 3) I checked whether some upstream screen prevents navigation here: the parent home offers "Learning planner" unconditionally (home.tsx:110) and the planner has no per-child gate. 4) I checked whether the family-scope case is the only reachable one — it is not; a child-scope request leaves the adult's membership intact. 5) I checked that `plannerError` is not shared with a screen that does have pull-to-refresh: its only importer is app/(parent)/planner.tsx, so the 'Pull to refresh' string is wrong on its only surface.
findings.suggested_fix: In `ChildPlan`, branch on `child.deletionPending === true` before computing `editable` and before either `useLoad`, returning the same notice the Children screen and the web planner use ("Data deletion under way. A deletion request covering {nickname}'s data is open. Processing has already stopped, so no practice is prepared or released for them and their plan is not kept…" plus the Privacy and Contact support routes), and make no request. Label the child in the `<Choice>` options the way the web picker does (`childPickerSuffix` → ' (data deletion under way)'). Separately, change the NOT_FOUND text in src/learning/planner-form.ts to offer the screen's own "Try again" instead of a pull gesture the planner does not have.
findings.reproduction: apps/mobile/src/family/screens.test.ts (the HUNT6-H-1 describe block that already reads planner.tsx) — assert `planner` matches /child\.deletionPending === true/ and that the archived notice is not the branch a deletion-pending child reaches; and in src/learning/planner-form.test.ts assert the NOT_FOUND message does not match /pull to refresh/i. Both go red today.

findings.title: The planner's new archived read-only view keeps the "Coming up" card, so it tells the parent an archived child's daily practice is available today — the claim HUNT5-F-10 removed from the web planner in round 5
findings.claim_under_review: planner.tsx:155-156 — "{child.nickname} is archived, so their practice plan is read-only. Everything below is what was planned" — and planner.tsx:419-421, "An archived child's plan is shown, never offered for editing (HUNT6-H-1)".
findings.mechanism: The `!editable` early return (planner.tsx:422-446) renders `comingUp` (planner.tsx:406-417) as its first card. `comingUp` prints `buildUpcomingView(latest, childName)` (planner.tsx:380), whose `dailyLine` is one of 'Today's daily practice is available.', 'Today's daily practice opens <instant>.' or 'Daily practice is paused today.', and whose `reviewLines` are future per-subject release instants (apps/mobile/src/learning/planner-form.ts:201-220). Those values are computed live by the API for an archived profile too: GET /learning-schedule takes the `owned.archived` path (apps/api/src/routes/learning.ts:686-692) into `scheduleResponse`, which builds `nextReviewReleases` from `currentAndNextWeekKeys(now, zone)` and `dailyPractice.state` from `dailyPracticeState({now, …})` with no reference to the status (learning.ts:488-545). Nothing is released to an archived child: the archive transaction revokes every child session and device (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:535-539). The web planner records this exact defect and its fix: "HUNT5-F-10: this used to end 'and nothing here is released to them', which the schedule section below contradicts — it prints this child's next daily and weekly review instants, and nothing there branches on the status", and its copy now reads "no new practice is prepared for them … and the times below are what the schedule would produce if the profile were active again" (apps/web/src/pages/app/LearningPlannerPage.tsx:174-185). The mobile notice written this round carries neither half: it does not say no new practice is prepared, and it frames the times as "what was planned" when they are present- and future-tense release claims.
findings.impact: A parent who archived a child to free a paid slot opens that child's planner and reads "Coming up — Today's daily practice is available." and "Mathematics: Thu 16:00 (weekly review)". Neither will happen: the child's devices and sessions are revoked. The parent is told the child is still being given work, which is the opposite of what archiving does, and may leave the profile archived believing practice continues. The mobile and web planners now say different things about the same API response for the same child state, which is the surface mismatch the brief records as having been filed twice.
findings.ruled_out: 1) I checked that the API really returns live release times for an archived profile rather than empty arrays: `storedPlan` (learning.ts:468-486) still fills `subjects` from enabled `child_subjects`, and `scheduleResponse` filters only releases already in the past, so future instants are returned. 2) I checked whether the mobile notice's hedge covers it: 'Everything below is what was planned' describes stored settings; "Coming up" is a heading about the future and `dailyLine` is present tense, so the hedge does not reach it — and the web client judged the same hedge insufficient in HUNT5-F-10, which is why it added the explicit conditional. 3) I checked whether archiving cancels the schedule so the times would at least be absent: the archive route (family.ts:504-551) touches slots, status, sessions, devices and audit only — the schedule rows and test dates stay, so the times are always produced. 4) I checked the editable path: for an active or draft child the card is correct, so the defect is confined to the branch this round added.
findings.suggested_fix: In the `!editable` branch, either drop `comingUp` or reword the notice to carry both halves the web copy carries: that no new practice is prepared or released for an archived child, and that the times shown are what the schedule would produce if the profile were active again. Also add the slot condition the web copy states ("while a paid slot is free") to "make them active again in Children", since `childRows` only offers activation when `unusedPaidSlots(family) > 0` (family-view.ts:140).
findings.reproduction: apps/mobile/src/family/screens.test.ts, the 'the planner offers no write an archived child cannot take (HUNT6-H-1)' block — add an assertion that the archived notice matches /no new practice is prepared/i and /would produce/ (mirroring apps/web/src/pages/app/LearningPlannerPage.tsx), or that the `!editable` return does not render `comingUp`. Red today.

findings.title: The parent Rewards screen got only half of the HUNT6-I-2 fix: rows are dropped before the fetch, but no run ticket, so an older in-flight answer publishes over a newer one
findings.claim_under_review: src/family/ui.tsx:520-529 — "an ANSWER also has an owner … Every run takes a ticket and only the current ticket may publish; an older run's answer, and its error, are dropped" — asserted for the shared hook while rewards.tsx, which this round edited for the same finding, publishes whatever resolves last. Also rewards.tsx:97-98, "the list is stale: reload so no button stays on screen that can only fail."
findings.mechanism: rewards.tsx does not use `useLoad`; it owns its fetch. Round 6 added `setState({ status: 'loading' })` before `void load()` in the mount/identity effect (rewards.tsx:74-82) — half 1 of HUNT6-I-2 — but `load` itself (rewards.tsx:65-72) is still `setState({ status: 'ready', data: await loadRewardsOverview(api) })` with no run counter, which is exactly the unguarded publish the same commit removed from `useLoad` (ui.tsx:544-556) and from privacy.tsx (privacy.tsx:121-132, `latestLoad`/`ticket`). Four callers can overlap: the effect (:81), pull-to-refresh (:86), the error retry (:164) and the post-decision reload (:99). The post-decision path is the reachable one: `decide` clears `busy` at :96 BEFORE `await load()` at :99, so every button is live again while that reload is in flight; approving a second card starts a second decision and a second `load()`. Whichever request resolves last wins, so reload #1 can overwrite reload #2 and restore the list as it was before the second decision — with Approve/Decline still on a request the server has already decided. That is precisely the state RV-rewards-7's reload exists to prevent, per the comment at :97-98. The same unguarded publish is also the privacy leg the round-6 prose claims to have closed: when the gate publishes a new client for a new adult (ui.tsx:296-313), the effect starts B's load, and A's still-in-flight answer — fetched with A's bearer — publishes A's child nicknames, point balances and open reward requests as 'ready' under B's client.
findings.impact: A parent approving two reward requests in quick succession can be shown the pre-decision list with buttons that can only fail; tapping one produces a refusal the screen exists to avoid. In the handed-on-tablet case the previous family's child nicknames and point balances render for the next adult, which is the harm the round-6 fix was written for and left unclosed on this one screen. Nothing pins either half: `grep -n 'HUNT6-I-2\|loading' apps/mobile/src/rewards/review.test.ts` returns nothing, so the round-6 edit to this screen is untested.
findings.ruled_out: 1) I checked that rewards.tsx really keys on the gate's client, so the identity half is not also missing: `RewardApprovals({ api })` receives `access.api` (rewards.tsx:56) and `load` is `useCallback(…, [api])` (:72), which the HUNT6-I-1 walker does check. 2) I checked whether RefreshControl serialises the pulls — it does prevent a second pull while `refreshing` is true, which is why I based the mechanism on the decide→reload path, where nothing serialises: `busy` is cleared before the reload and pull-to-refresh does not set `busy` at all. 3) I checked whether `decideRequestAction` already re-renders from its own response instead of needing the list: it returns only `{ok, needsPin, reload, message}` (src/rewards/actions.ts:20-30), so the list on screen comes solely from `load`. 4) I checked whether the old client's request would simply fail after a handover: `createMobileApi` resolves the bearer when the request is made, so a request already in flight carries the previous adult's token and the server answers that family. 5) I checked privacy.tsx and useLoad, which both received the ticket, confirming this is an omission on one screen rather than a deliberate scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Give `load` the same ticket the sibling screens got: bump a `latestRun`/`latestLoad` ref before the await, capture it, and return without publishing (rows and error alike) when `latestRun.current !== ticket`. Add the repro to apps/mobile/src/rewards/review.test.ts as a source pin next to the other screen pins, mirroring the wording of the assertions in src/family/screens-r2.review.test.ts for `useLoad`.
findings.reproduction: apps/mobile/src/rewards/review.test.ts — add, in the style of src/family/screens-r2.review.test.ts's useLoad block, `expect(parentRewardsScreen).toMatch(/const ticket = latest(Run|Load)\.current;/)` and `expect(parentRewardsScreen).not.toMatch(/setState\(\{ status: 'ready', data: await loadRewardsOverview\(api\) \}\)/)`. Both go red today.

findings.title: The HUNT6-I-1 keying guard says "no parent screen can opt out silently" but only inspects useCallback/useEffect in app/(parent)/*.tsx and only the identifiers `api` and `load`; the shape it was written for can come back outside all three limits
findings.claim_under_review: screens-r2.review.test.ts:345-357 — "So the premise is asserted rather than assumed, over EVERY parent screen: a hook that reads the gate's client, or calls a loader closed over it, must list it, so a new client re-runs the load. A screen added later cannot opt out silently."
findings.mechanism: `hooks()` (screens-r2.review.test.ts:375-401) scans only `/\buse(?:Callback|Effect)\(/`, and the offender loop (:402-413) only looks for the bare identifiers 'api' and 'load'. Three ways to satisfy the test while breaking the property: (a) a screen-local loader hook whose body lives OUTSIDE app/(parent)/ — the walker only reads `readdirSync(parentDir)` (:359-361), so `const family = useApiLoad(() => api.get('/v1/family', schema), 'family')` imported from src/ has no useCallback/useEffect in the screen to inspect and reports zero offenders; that is exactly the shape HUNT6-I-1 found in planner.tsx, differing only in where the helper is declared; (b) a `useMemo` loader — not in the regex, and privacy.tsx already builds its client in a `useMemo` (privacy.tsx:90), so the shape is in use in this directory; (c) a client bound under another name (`client`, `parentApi`, a destructured `{ api: gateApi }`), which neither identifier matches. The companion guard meant to stop a vacuous pass — "the screens really do go through the shared hook" (:418-424) — names only children.tsx, home.tsx, planner.tsx and devices.tsx, i.e. 4 of the 13 files in app/(parent)/; privacy.tsx, rewards.tsx and resources.tsx genuinely do not use `useLoad` at all, so the set the guard vouches for is the set that already passes.
findings.impact: The enforcement that BUG-335 was closed with is narrower than its own sentence. A future screen, or a refactor that moves a loader helper into src/, reinstates the handed-on-tablet defect with a green suite — and the same suite is the only thing standing behind a premise the project has had to re-fix in three consecutive rounds. No parent is harmed today: I enumerated all 13 files in app/(parent)/ and every data loader currently keys on the gate's client (or, for privacy.tsx, on the module token source, which gets a fresh closure per auth change in src/lib/app-session.ts:58-63), so nothing is presently exempt.
findings.ruled_out: 1) I checked the test is not merely decorative in the shape-2 sense: reverting the planner to its round-5 `useApiLoad` (whose useEffect body used `load` with deps `[key, version]`) does make it red, so it catches the literal regression it was written for. The defect is the gap between that and the sentence it states. 2) I checked whether any current screen already exploits a gap, which would make this a MEDIUM: none does — plan.tsx:70 and resources.tsx:94/181/256 use `useMemo` for a store, a viewport, a locale and a view model, never for a fetch. 3) I checked whether `code()` (:364-370) could make the walker miss a real hook by mangling source: it strips comments and single/double-quoted strings but not template literals; the templates in these screens are balanced, so no current hook is lost. 4) I confirmed the walker does cover privacy.tsx, rewards.tsx and resources.tsx for the hooks they do use, so the name-based check is load-bearing for them and my finding is about the shapes it cannot see, not about those screens.
findings.suggested_fix: Widen the walker to `use[A-Z]\w*\(` (any hook call) rather than useCallback/useEffect, and derive the client identifier from the screen instead of hard-coding 'api'/'load' — e.g. require that any hook whose body calls `.get(`/`.send(` or a `load*`/`use*Load` helper lists every in-scope identifier it closes over. Extend the second guard to require `useLoad(` in every screen that makes a request, and list the deliberate exceptions (privacy.tsx, rewards.tsx, resources.tsx) by name with the per-screen assertion each one needs instead, so a new screen is not silently an exception.
findings.reproduction: apps/mobile/src/family/screens-r2.review.test.ts, the '[repro] no parent screen has a load hook that a new client cannot re-run' case: move planner.tsx's loaders behind a helper declared in src/family/ui.tsx whose effect deps are `[]`. The suite stays green while the planner stops refetching for a new adult — which is BUG-335 reproduced past the guard.

findings.title: The planner's schedule reload after a subject toggle changes nothing on screen: ScheduleEditor captures `initial` in useState once and has no key
findings.claim_under_review: planner.tsx:178-181 — `onChanged={() => { void subjects.reload(); void schedule.reload(); }}` — the schedule reload exists so the "Coming up" releases follow a subject change; it cannot.
findings.mechanism: `ScheduleEditor` seeds all of its display state from the prop once: `const [latest, setLatest] = useState(initial)` (planner.tsx:372) and `const [form, setForm] = useState(() => scheduleToPlannerForm(initial.schedule))` (:373), and `comingUp` is built from `latest` (:380, :406-417). It is mounted at planner.tsx:195-201 with no `key`, so when `schedule.reload()` resolves and `schedule.state.data` becomes a new object, React reuses the instance and `useState` ignores the new `initial`. `nextReviewReleases` is computed from the child's ENABLED subjects (apps/api/src/routes/learning.ts:475-484, 501-521), so it is exactly the field a subject toggle changes — and the only value the reload was added to refresh. Only `save()` updates it, via `setLatest(saved)` (:395).
findings.impact: A parent turns Mathematics off in Subjects; the toggle row flips to 'Off' (SubjectToggles renders its prop), but the "Coming up" card keeps listing "Mathematics: <instant> (weekly review)" until the child is switched or the screen is remounted. The parent is shown a review that will not be generated, and the wasted GET runs on every toggle.
findings.ruled_out: 1) I checked whether `ChildPlan`'s `key={child.id}` (planner.tsx:117) remounts the editor — it only remounts on a child change, not on a reload of the same child. 2) I checked whether `useLoad`'s reload could return the same object identity and so be a no-op anyway: `run` always calls `setState({ status: 'ready', data })` with a fresh object (src/family/ui.tsx:549), so the prop really does change and only the useState capture swallows it. 3) I checked that the reload is not redundant for another reason: `nextReviewReleases` genuinely depends on enabled subjects, so the data does change server-side. 4) I checked the archived branch: it has no toggle, so no reload, so no staleness there — the defect is confined to the editable path. 5) This is pre-existing rather than introduced this round; I am filing it because the round-6 change lifted `comingUp` out of the editable branch and made it the first thing both branches render, so the stale card is now the card an archived child's whole view is built around.
findings.suggested_fix: Either give `<ScheduleEditor>` a key derived from the loaded schedule (e.g. the daily/review fields or a reload counter) so a reload remounts it, or render `comingUp` from `schedule.state.data` in `ChildPlan` rather than from the editor's captured `latest`, leaving `form`/`latest` as edit state only.
findings.reproduction: apps/mobile/src/family/screens.test.ts — pin that the "Coming up" card is built from the loaded schedule and not from `latest`: assert planner.tsx matches /buildUpcomingView\(schedule\.state\.data/ or that `<ScheduleEditor` carries a key. Red today.

findings.title: The privacy screen's load takes its ticket AFTER the `!api` early return, so a load that finds no client does not supersede an in-flight one and the previous session's answer can still publish
findings.claim_under_review: privacy.tsx:123-128 — "A load superseded while its request was in flight publishes nothing. Two ways to be superseded: a newer load, which for this screen means a new client and so the next adult at the device …"
findings.mechanism: `load` (privacy.tsx:115-133) returns at :118-121 when `api` is null, before `latestLoad.current += 1` at :122. So a run that finds no client sets `{status:'not_connected'}` but leaves `latestLoad.current` pointing at the PREVIOUS run's ticket. An earlier load that is still in flight therefore still satisfies `latestLoad.current === ticket` when it resolves and publishes `{status:'ready', data}` (:129) over the 'not_connected' state. The path: the parent session ends elsewhere (portal "sign out everywhere", a password change), `parentAuth.watch` sets the registered privacy source to null (src/lib/app-session.ts:58-63), and the next re-render makes `api` null so the effect at :139-150 fires with `access.status` still 'ready' (the gate deliberately does not re-check on `parentAuth.watch`, src/family/ui.tsx:340-349). The earlier request then repaints the signed-out family's children, exports and safety reports.
findings.impact: On a device whose parent session has just been revoked, the privacy screen can flip from the honest "not connected" state back to a full render of that family's children, export list and safety reports until a focus or foreground event re-gates the screen. It is a narrow window and needs a specific interleaving, but it is the one door in this screen's ticket that is not covered, and safety reports are the most sensitive rows the parent area holds.
findings.ruled_out: 1) I checked whether the closure guard already covers it: `closureStarted.current` is only set by `runAccountClosure` (privacy.tsx:198-208), so an ordinary session loss does not set it and the publish is not blocked there. 2) I checked whether the gate closes the screen first: `useParentAccess` re-checks only on mount, AppState 'active' and focus (ui.tsx:319-350) and explicitly does NOT re-check on `parentAuth.watch`, so `access.status` can stay 'ready' with no client. 3) I checked the harmful cross-ADULT variant — a new non-null client from a different adult — and it is correctly covered, because that load does reach :122 and bumps the ticket. 4) I checked that no other caller of `load` bypasses the ticket: `refresh` (:152), the error retry (:328) and the three post-action reloads all go through the same function. 5) I confirmed the render does not otherwise protect it: `{data ? …}` is driven by `state`, so a published 'ready' renders every section.
findings.suggested_fix: Bump `latestLoad` and capture the ticket as the FIRST thing `load` does, before the `closureStarted` and `!api` returns, so every entry into `load` supersedes whatever is in flight — the same ordering `useLoad` uses (src/family/ui.tsx:539-542, where the ticket is taken before anything can be awaited).
findings.reproduction: apps/mobile/src/family/screens.test.ts, the 'the parent privacy screen goes through the same gate' case — assert that in the `load` body `const ticket = latestLoad.current;` appears before `if (!api) {`. Red today.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: HUNT6-I-1: every parent screen keys its load on the client the gate published, so a new adult always causes a refetch (the premise BUG-335 broke).
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Enumerated all 13 files in apps/mobile/app/(parent)/ and wrote down, for each, what its load is keyed on and where the refetch happens: children.tsx:62 useLoad(useCallback(…,[api])); home.tsx:49-57 same; devices.tsx:40-47 same; planner.tsx:80 and 138-147 same (now through useLoad, keyed [api] and [api, base]); plan.tsx:71 and :443 same; school.tsx:109 and :508 ([api, version]); support.tsx:75, :164, :363, :366 same; rewards.tsx:65-82 own fetch keyed [api] via the gate's client; resources.tsx:210-227 own effect with deps [api, filters, platform, locale, version]; privacy.tsx:115-150 own loader keyed on a useMemo'd client derived from the module token source; pair-device.tsx, sign-in.tsx, unlock.tsx and _layout.tsx make no keyed data load. Then attacked the one screen not keyed on the gate's client at all — privacy.tsx — by tracing whether its `parentPrivacyTokenSource()` can stay identical across an adult change.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: No screen keys on nothing or on a value stable across a family change. privacy.tsx holds because src/lib/app-session.ts:58-63 builds a FRESH `parentSourceOutsideChildMode` closure on every auth change and re-registers it, so the module source changes identity for a new adult; the gate publishing a new 'ready' object (ui.tsx:296-313) forces the re-render that reads it, which changes `api` (:90), which changes `load` (:133), which re-runs the effect (:150). The only thing I could break there was a narrow in-flight case, filed as HUNT7-J-7.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: HUNT6-I-1 half 2: the planner's child selection is derived from the loaded family, so no family and no stale pick can leave the screen blank or put a non-option in the <Choice>.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Tried to construct a render with no branch: (a) a pick from the previous family with `children` non-empty — `childId` falls back to `children[0].id` (planner.tsx:88), so `child` resolves and ChildPlan renders; (b) `children` empty and `picked` non-null — `childId` is null, `children.length > 1` is false so no <Choice>, and the `ready && length === 0` Notice renders; (c) the <Choice>'s value — it is `childId`, which is provably a member of `children` or null, and `onChange` is the only writer of `picked`; (d) `ChildPlan key={child.id}` across a family change — the id differs, so schedule/subjects state cannot survive into the next family; (e) a family whose only child is deletion-pending — still renders a Heading, a Notice and two error boxes, so not blank (its content is wrong for other reasons, filed as HUNT7-J-2).
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: The derivation at planner.tsx:88-89 makes the invalid state unrepresentable, and the four render branches at :93-118 partition idle/loading, error, ready-with-none and ready-with-children. `setPicked` has exactly one caller, the <Choice>'s onChange, as the test at screens-r2.review.test.ts:452 pins.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: HUNT6-I-2 inside useLoad: rows produced by a different load are dropped BEFORE the new fetch, and no superseded answer or error is ever published.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Re-derived the two mistakes the round-5/6 history warns about. (a) The updater-reads-the-ref bug: `producedBy.current` is captured into `producer` before the setter and the new owner recorded before it (ui.tsx:551-553), so the updater compares the old owner, not itself. (b) The ticket: `latestRun.current += 1; const ticket = …` is taken before any await (ui.tsx:539-541) and re-checked on both the success and the catch path (:547, :553). (c) Tried a manual reload — `producer === load`, so `loadStateForRun` returns the same state object and nothing flashes (family-view.ts:42-48). (d) Tried `useLoad(null)`, where the ticket is skipped and the state is never reset: grepped every caller (14 call sites, all passing a non-null useCallback), so the branch is unreachable. (e) Tried an unmount mid-request and a same-tick double reload.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: Every publish is behind the ticket, the ownership check reads a value captured before the setter, and no caller can reach the null branch. The rule itself is a pure function with value-in/value-out tests (family-view.test.ts:215-238), so it is not only grepped. The hook is sound; what broke is the screen that does not use it (HUNT7-J-4).

properties_attacked_and_held.property: HUNT6-J-2: once the closure has started, the whole "Delete my account" section is off the screen for the length of the operation, through every door.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Enumerated every door into `load` and every renderer of the section. Doors: the reload effect (privacy.tsx:139-150, guarded by `closureStarted`), pull-to-refresh (:152-156 → `load`, guarded inside `load` at :117), the error retry button (:328-332 → `load`), and the three post-action reloads in requestExport/requestDeletion/actOnReport (:172, :224, :236) — all go through the one guarded `load`. Renderers: the section is inside `{data ? …}` (:526) and `data` is null unless `state.status === 'ready'` (:238), which `closureStarted` prevents. Tried reaching the error-retry button during a closure (it renders only for `state.status === 'error'`, a state `closeAccount` cannot start from, since the button itself only exists in 'ready'). Tried the api→null re-render caused by the sign-out inside the closure un-registering the token source — the effect leaves early on `closureStarted`. Tried a second tap of "Delete my account" during the API call — `busy !== null` (:194) and `disabled={busy !== null}` (:556) block it, and the state leaves 'ready' the moment the server answers (src/privacy/parent-privacy.ts runAccountClosure step 'closing').
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: The guard is in `load`, which is the single path to `state = 'ready'`, and the section's visibility is derived from that state rather than from a busy flag — so no gesture, retry or re-render can put a second live delete button back. The pull gesture is additionally not offered at all while 'closing'/'account_closed' (:266-272).

properties_attacked_and_held.property: HUNT6-H-1: no planner control is offered for a write the API refuses, and an archived child's stored plan stays readable.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Checked the API first: `ownedChild(c,'write')` throws `archivedChild()` for status 'archived' and leaves 'draft' writable (apps/api/src/routes/learning.ts:209-211), which matches `childPlanEditable` exactly (family-view.ts:76-78, tested at family-view.test.ts:248-254). Then hunted for a surviving write control on the archived path: the Switch is behind `editable` (planner.tsx:256-264), the Save button behind `editable` (:540-546), and the whole field set is replaced by a read-only summary (:422-446) so there is nothing to type into; the pause ToggleRow, the Steppers and the Fields exist only in the editable return. Also checked the reads the screen depends on for an archived child really succeed (learning.ts:622-625 and :686-692 both have an archived path).
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: For status 'archived' the mapping is exact and every control is omitted rather than disabled, so there is no Save the server would refuse and nothing typed to lose. It broke only for the case the status hides — a deletion-pending child, which request_deletion also marks 'archived' but whose READS the API refuses too (filed as HUNT7-J-2).

properties_attacked_and_held.property: HUNT6-I-3: the Children screen's deletion notice says only what `deletionPending` carries, and never tells the reader THEY asked for the deletion.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Read the flag's computation (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:215-222: scope/target only, no requested_by) and then read the notice word by word (children.tsx:252-258) looking for a residual requester claim, including the closing "if you did not mean it, contact support straight away" and the "whole family" hedge HUNT5-H-3 removed. Checked that the negative assertions are not weaker than they look: children-screen.test.ts:106-111 scopes them to the notice (so the screen's legitimate "Cancel edit" is excluded) and asserts the notice is non-empty first, so the guard cannot pass over an empty capture (L-054).
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: The sentence is requester-neutral and scope-true; "if you did not mean it" is conditional and addressed to whichever adult might have asked, so it asserts nothing about the reader. Both the notice assertions and the anti-vacuity check are present in two suites. What is false on that screen is the status line above the notice, not the notice (filed as HUNT7-J-1).

properties_attacked_and_held.property: HUNT6-I-4: the screen-privacy change the lock defers is settled only by callers that know the app is in the foreground, and the Lock button is one of them.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Traced the new `.then(() => settleChildSpaceScreenPrivacy(modeEffects))` on the Lock button (ui.tsx:371-385) against `lockParentAreaOnDevice` (src/lib/mode.ts:180-217) and the 'active' handler (src/lib/app-session.ts:98-104). Attacked: (a) a rejection of `lockParentAreaOnDevice` skipping `.then` — the only statement that can throw uncaught is `resetNavigationToChildHome()`, which runs before the debt is recorded, so the debt is simply never taken and the child space keeps adult protection; (b) a background→immediate-active race, where 'active' settles before `childSpaceOwedScreenPrivacyOff = true` is reached (it is set after two awaits); (c) the debt surviving forever — `settleChildSpaceScreenPrivacy` clears it before the call, so an OS refusal is not retried, as documented.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: Both races leave the debt TRUE rather than falsely settled, and mode is then 'child', so the next foreground event settles it and the failure mode is a temporary over-protection of the child space, never an under-protection of the adult frame — the direction the fix exists to protect. I did not file it: it is self-healing and lives in mode.ts / app-session.ts, outside this area. The one real cost I could measure is that the Lock button now settles only after `relockOnServer()` is awaited, so on a slow or offline network a paired tablet keeps capture blocked in the child space for up to the request timeout.

findings.title: `secretsCleared` reports that neither device secret was actually removed: both clears still swallow the failure that matters, so the closure copy withholds its caveat in exactly the case the caveat exists for
findings.claim_under_review: `secretsCleared` is whether both device clears succeeded. Neither fact is "nothing threw", which is all the previous version could observe. (parent-privacy.ts:181-182) — and, in mode.ts:34-35, "The parent's biometric PIN and the store SDK identity were both removed from this device." — and, in runtime.ts:220-221, "both are now REPORTED rather than discarded (HUNT6-J-1) … Answers whether both succeeded."
findings.mechanism: accountClosedDeviceMessage (apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.ts:194) takes the clean `ACCOUNT_CLOSE_COPY.closed`/`.pending` branch only when `device.secretsCleared` is true, and otherwise adds 'This device is signed out, but we could not remove everything this app had saved for your account. Removing the app removes the rest.' (parent-privacy.ts:201-203). `secretsCleared` comes from apps/mobile/src/family/runtime.ts:223-233 `clearDeviceAdultSecrets()`, which round 6 converted from `.catch(() => undefined)` to `.then(() => true, () => false)` on two calls — but it converted only the OUTER wrappers, and both of those wrappers still swallow the failure of the operation the flag names. (a) `biometricPinStore.clear` is `clearBiometricPin` (runtime.ts:75-79): its first line is `await SecureStore.deleteItemAsync(BIOMETRIC_PIN_KEY).catch(() => undefined);`, so a failure to delete the PIN ITEM is discarded and the function still resolves as long as the two plain flag deletes (BIOMETRIC_ENABLED_KEY, BIOMETRIC_OWNER_KEY) succeed — `pinCleared` therefore proves 'the two flags were deleted', which is the fact adjacent to 'the PIN was removed'. (b) `forgetStoreIdentity()` (apps/mobile/src/billing/revenuecat.ts:125-133) ends in `await Purchases.logOut().catch(() => undefined);`, so `storeForgotten` proves 'a module-local map was cleared and the mutex resolved', not that the store SDK forgot the identity. The composite `pinCleared && storeForgotten` is therefore true whenever the two SecureStore flag deletes resolve, which is the same 'no keychain write threw' predicate HUNT6-J-1 was filed to remove — one layer further in. This is shape 6 as well: `clearBiometricPin` was written as a best-effort helper (it is also called by the biometric-disable path and by `biometricPinStore.isEnabled()`'s 'other_user' cleanup, where swallowing is correct), and round 6 gave its resolution a second job — 'the PIN was removed' — without changing it.
findings.impact: On a device whose keychain refuses the PIN item specifically (or whose store SDK logout fails), a parent who has just deleted their account reads 'Your PencilLift account is closed and this device is signed out.' and is NOT shown the sentence the round added for that case — 'we could not remove everything this app had saved for your account. Removing the app removes the rest.' — so they leave the app installed with their 6-digit parent PIN still in the device keychain and the store SDK still bound to the closed account's app user id. The same flag is the one thing standing behind the round's stated guarantee that the closure copy rests on reported facts rather than on nothing having thrown.
findings.ruled_out: (1) I checked whether the leftover PIN is still usable: it is not directly — `clearBiometricPin` deletes BIOMETRIC_ENABLED_KEY before returning, so `biometricOffer({enabled:false,…})` returns 'off' (apps/mobile/src/family/unlock.ts:38) and `biometricPinStore.isEnabled()` withholds the offer, so the stale PIN cannot be submitted through the app. That bounds the finding to a retained secret plus the withheld caveat; it does not remove it, because the caveat sentence exists precisely to tell the parent that something the app saved stayed behind. (2) I checked whether a keychain fault would fail all three deletes and so report correctly anyway: BIOMETRIC_ENABLED_KEY/BIOMETRIC_OWNER_KEY go through apps/mobile/src/lib/secure-storage.ts, which is the same `SecureStore.deleteItemAsync`, so a store-wide outage does set the flag false — the hole is the asymmetric case, and it is the plausible one, because BIOMETRIC_PIN_KEY is the only item written with `requireAuthentication: true` and `WHEN_PASSCODE_SET_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY` (runtime.ts:109-113) and expo-secure-store documents deletes as able to reject. (3) I checked whether the store half self-heals: `forgetStoreIdentity` sets `identifiedAs = null` before the logOut, so the next identify re-binds — that softens the store half but not the PIN half, and the parent is still not told. (4) I verified the sibling flag is sound, so this is not a blanket complaint: `sessionEndConfirmed` really does observe the session removal — auth-js 2.116 `_signOut` returns `{error}` only after `removeCurrentSession()`, `_removeSession` awaits `removeItemAsync` unguarded, and apps/mobile/src/lib/chunked-storage.ts:150-157 `removeItem` propagates every `store.deleteItem` rejection, so a failed keychain removal reaches `parentAuth.signOut`'s catch and becomes `ok:false`. (5) No test covers this: apps/mobile/src/family/screens-r2.review.test.ts:119 only greps that `clearDeviceAdultSecrets` mentions `biometricPinStore.clear()`, and parent-privacy.test.ts:337-345 feeds `secretsCleared:false` in directly rather than producing it.
findings.reproduction: No test today can go red, which is part of the finding: `clearDeviceAdultSecrets` is module-private and only source-grepped (apps/mobile/src/family/screens-r2.review.test.ts:116-140). A regression test belongs next to runtime.ts with `expo-secure-store` and `../billing/revenuecat.ts` mocked: make `SecureStore.deleteItemAsync(BIOMETRIC_PIN_KEY)` reject while `secureStorage.deleteItem` resolves, and assert `signOutClosedAccountOnDevice()` answers `secretsCleared: false`; then assert `accountClosedDeviceMessage('closed', outcome)` matches /could not remove everything/i. Both assertions fail today (the first returns true, the second returns ACCOUNT_CLOSE_COPY.closed).
findings.suggested_fix: Make the two inner helpers answer instead of swallowing, and keep the best-effort contract at the caller. Give `clearBiometricPin` a boolean-ish result (or a separate reporting wrapper) so the `SecureStore.deleteItemAsync(BIOMETRIC_PIN_KEY)` rejection becomes part of what `biometricPinStore.clear()` reports, without letting it stop the two flag deletes; do the same for `Purchases.logOut()` inside `forgetStoreIdentity` (report it, still never throw). Then `clearDeviceAdultSecrets` can keep `pinCleared && storeForgotten` and mean it. If the store half is judged unobservable, say so in the JSDoc and drop it from what `secretsCleared` claims rather than leaving the sentence as it is.

findings.title: The child scan screen keeps claiming "Sending page N of M…" with a live "Stop sending" for the whole cancel round trip — HUNT6-J-2's defect on the child surface, left unfixed in the round that named it
findings.claim_under_review: HUNT6-J-2's principle as the round applied it on the parent surface: "The 'closing' step comes BEFORE the device sign-out … The screen used to clear its busy flag as soon as the API answered and set its outcome only after the sign-out, so for that whole window it looked idle with every control live" (apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.ts:225-232). The child abort path is the same shape and was not changed.
findings.mechanism: In `send()`'s abort branch the screen awaits the cancel and only then leaves the running state: `const outcome = stoppedScanOutcome(await cancelScan(childApi, attemptRef.current)); … setUpload({ kind: 'error', message: outcome.message });` (apps/mobile/app/(child)/scan.tsx:286-288). Nothing between the child's tap and that await changes state — the Stop button is `onPress={() => controllerRef.current?.abort()}` (scan.tsx:513) and abort() sets no React state. So for the length of `cancelScan`'s POST the screen still renders `upload.kind === 'running'`: the frozen progress line `progressText(upload.progress)` ("Sending page 2 of 3…", scan.tsx:70-81, 493), the progress bar, and the same live "Stop sending" button. That POST goes through `childApi` with no request options, so it runs to `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000` (packages/contracts/src/client.ts:49, 116) before answering 'unsure'; and `childApi` is `withChildTokenRetry(...)` (apps/mobile/src/homework/child-api.ts:18), which re-runs the call once on a single UNAUTHENTICATED answer (apps/mobile/src/family/child-session.ts:101-110), so a second full attempt can follow. Because `running` is also what hides the page controls and the Send button (scan.tsx:379, 451, 523), the child cannot do anything else either: the only control on screen is the one that now does nothing (a second `abort()` on an already-aborted controller is a no-op).
findings.impact: A child aged 5-13 taps "Stop sending" on a flaky connection and the screen goes on telling them their homework is being sent, with the Stop button still offered, for up to twenty seconds per attempt — the exact "nothing happened, press it again" experience HUNT6-J-2 identified as the defect on the parent closure screen. The progress text is false while it is shown: the send has already been aborted locally. Nothing else on the screen is reachable during that window.
findings.ruled_out: (1) I checked for money harm and there is none: the Send/"Try again" button is not rendered while `running`, so no second `send()` and no second assignment can be started from this window, and repeated `abort()` calls cannot issue a second cancel — `cancelScan` is called once, from the catch. That is why this is medium and not high. (2) I checked that the window is real rather than instantaneous: it is skipped only when `attempt.assignmentId === null`, where `cancelScan` returns 'nothing_to_cancel' without any request (apps/mobile/src/homework/upload.ts:147) — i.e. the delay happens exactly when a scan really was created, the case that matters. (3) I checked that the 20 s figure is not overridden: `createMobileApi` passes no `ApiClientOptions` (apps/mobile/src/lib/api.ts:11-13), so the default applies, and the cancel passes no per-request timeout (upload.ts:149-154). (4) I checked whether some other state already acknowledges the tap: there is no 'stopping' state in `UploadState` (scan.tsx:60-64) and `setNotice` is not called on abort. (5) I checked that this is not out of scope as "pre-existing": the `await cancelScan` in the abort path is what round 5 put there and what round 6 re-read and re-documented (scan.tsx:127-131 and the HUNT6-J-7 suite in apps/mobile/src/homework/scan-screen.test.ts:98-123), and the round-6 diff fixed the identical shape on the parent surface in the same commit.
findings.reproduction: No test can go red today, because apps/mobile/src/homework/scan-screen.test.ts only reads scan.tsx as text — its `abortBranch` regex (lines 60-63) asserts the branch's spelling, not its timing, which is precisely the weakness HUNT6-J-2 called out on the parent side ("the previous check grepped the screen for the await and the ternary, which both orderings satisfy"). The fix should follow HUNT6-J-2: lift the abort path into a pure `runStoppedScan(api, attempt, step)` in apps/mobile/src/homework/upload.ts and assert in apps/mobile/src/homework/upload.test.ts that a `stopping` step is emitted before a `cancelScan` that never settles answers — that assertion fails against today's code.
findings.suggested_fix: Acknowledge the tap before the network call: add a `{ kind: 'stopping' }` state to `UploadState`, set it from the Stop button (or at the top of the abort branch, before the await), render calm child copy for it ("Stopping…") with no progress claim and no live Stop button, and set the final `{ kind: 'error', message: outcome.message }` when `cancelScan` answers. Move the decision into src/homework so the order is run in a unit test rather than grepped, the way `runAccountClosure` did for the parent screen. Do not shorten or skip the cancel, and do not drop the awaited answer — the answer is what keeps "one job, one charge" honest.

findings.title: parent-auth.ts's new JSDoc states the opposite of what auth-js does, and the opposite of what its own test, mode.ts and parent-privacy.ts all say
findings.claim_under_review: "supabase-js does not throw for a refused or failed sign-out; it returns the failure in `{ error }`, and when the logout call failed it does not remove the local session either — so dropping that `error` left a device still holding the parent's session with nothing in the app able to tell. `ok: false` means this device may still be signed in." (apps/mobile/src/lib/parent-auth.ts:118-122)
findings.mechanism: The middle clause is false for the case it describes. In auth-js 2.116 `_signOut` (node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+auth-js@2.116.0/…/dist/main/GoTrueClient.js:3422-3452), when `this.admin.signOut(accessToken, scope)` returns an error that is not 404/401/403/session-missing, and `scope !== 'others'` (this app passes 'local', parent-auth.ts:128), it calls `removeCurrentSession()` and only THEN returns `{ error }`. A fetch failure takes the same route: `GoTrueAdminApi.signOut` catches and returns `{ error }` for any `isAuthError` (dist/main/GoTrueAdminApi.js:67-85), and `AuthRetryableFetchError` is not an AuthApiError, so the removal runs. The session is therefore gone from the keychain in both failure shapes the file's own tests exercise. The only path that returns an error WITHOUT removing is the early `sessionError` return — the stored session could not be read or refreshed — which is a different fact from "the logout call failed". Three other places in the tree state this correctly and contradict this file: apps/mobile/src/lib/parent-auth.test.ts:169-173 ("auth-js 2.116 removes the LOCAL session even when the logout call failed, so this is 'the service was not told', not 'the device is still signed in'", and it asserts `await parentAuth.userId()` is null after a 500 on /logout); apps/mobile/src/lib/mode.ts:26-31; and apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.ts:176-179. Per L-053 the test and those two comments are TRUE and parent-auth.ts:118-122 is the one that is wrong.
findings.impact: No runtime effect. The harm is to the next reader of the only wrapper that decides what the app may claim about a signed-out device: the sentence justifies `ok: false` as "this device may still be signed in", which is the overstatement HUNT6-J-1's own fix removed from the parent-facing copy ('We could not sign this device out.' was replaced by 'We could not confirm this device is signed out.'). A maintainer reasoning from this file rather than from mode.ts would put that overstatement back, and would do it in the file whose stated danger is a false claim about the device the parent is holding.
findings.ruled_out: (1) I read the installed library rather than trusting memory, in both the client and the admin API, and traced both the HTTP-error and the fetch-rejection paths. (2) I checked that the sentence is not salvaged by an edge case: the early `sessionError` return does leave the stored session in place, so the FINAL sentence ('may still be signed in') is defensible — which is why I am filing the middle clause, not the whole block, and why the fix is a rewording rather than a code change. (3) I checked that the code itself is right: `signOut` returns `{ok:false}` for both a returned `{error}` and a thrown error (parent-auth.ts:127-132), and `signOutParent` consumes `.ok` without re-swallowing it (apps/mobile/src/lib/mode.ts:322-325), so the reported fact reaches the screen — the defect here is prose only. (4) I checked that no test pins the wrong sentence: parent-auth.test.ts asserts on behaviour, not on this comment, so a reword turns nothing red.
findings.reproduction: apps/mobile/src/lib/parent-auth.test.ts:160-174 is the reproduction as it stands: it makes /logout answer 500, gets `ok:false`, and then asserts `expect(await parentAuth.userId()).toBeNull()` — i.e. it proves the local session WAS removed, which is what parent-auth.ts:119-120 says does not happen. The file's own suite already contradicts the file's own comment.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword parent-auth.ts:118-122 to the fact the code has, matching mode.ts:23-32: supabase-js reports a refused or failed sign-out in `{ error }` rather than throwing, and (auth-js 2.116) still removes the local session in that case — it does not remove it only when it could not read the session at all. So `ok: false` means this device cannot say the session ended, not that it is still signed in; the caller must keep going regardless, and the copy may claim neither state.

findings.title: `closeAccountAction` still manufactures the unconditional "and this device is signed out" message that nothing reads any more, and a test pins it as required output
findings.claim_under_review: The JSDoc kept above `closeAccountAction` — "`closed` and `pending` both mean the device must sign out now (the API's signOut flag)" (apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.ts:258-261) — and the test assertion `message: expect.stringMatching(/account is closed and this device is signed out/i)` (apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.test.ts:475-478).
findings.mechanism: Round 6 moved the decision of what the parent reads into `runAccountClosure`, which uses only `result.status` and computes the sentence itself with `accountClosedDeviceMessage(result.status, device)` (parent-privacy.ts:239-254). `closeAccountAction` nevertheless still builds `message: result.status === 'closed' ? ACCOUNT_CLOSE_COPY.closed : ACCOUNT_CLOSE_COPY.pending` (parent-privacy.ts:275-278), and `ACCOUNT_CLOSE_COPY.closed` is 'Your PencilLift account is closed and this device is signed out.' (packages/contracts/src/account.ts:58). I grepped the whole tree: `closeAccountAction` has exactly one production caller, `runAccountClosure` (parent-privacy.ts:239), so for the two success statuses that `message` is now unreachable output — an incomplete removal that leaves the pre-HUNT5-N6 sentence sitting in the function a future caller would naturally read, still blessed by a JSDoc line that presents the status alone as meaning the device signs out. The test at parent-privacy.test.ts:475-478 asserts that exact unconditional sentence is returned, so the correct cleanup (dropping the dead field) turns a green test red, and the test itself passes regardless of anything the parent can see — it would stay green if `accountClosedDeviceMessage` were reverted to printing that sentence unconditionally, which is the failure it exists to prevent.
findings.impact: No user-visible effect today. It is the round-7 shape 7 trap on the screen where the round's whole point was that this sentence may not be said unconditionally: the string is still produced, still reachable by field access, still documented as what the status means, and a test makes removing it look like a regression.
findings.ruled_out: (1) I grepped for every caller of `closeAccountAction` across apps/mobile and apps/web before calling the field dead: only `runAccountClosure` and the test suite. (2) I checked that `runAccountClosure` really ignores it — it destructures nothing and passes only `result.status` (parent-privacy.ts:254), and the screen renders `step.message` from the step, not from the action (apps/mobile/app/(parent)/privacy.tsx:197-207). (3) I checked whether the error/step_up messages are also dead: they are not — `{status:'error'}` messages are shown as feedback via the 'refused' step, so the fix must keep those and touch only the two success statuses. (4) I checked whether the schema forces the field: `closeAccountResponseSchema`'s `signOut` flag is not read by the client at all, so nothing in contracts requires the message either. (5) I confirmed no other test would break: the only assertions on the success `message` are parent-privacy.test.ts:475-478 and 484-487.
findings.reproduction: apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.test.ts:475-478 is the test that would have to change: it asserts `closeAccountAction` returns /account is closed and this device is signed out/i, which nothing shows a parent. Deleting the dead `message` for 'closed'/'pending' makes that assertion fail, which is the signal that it was pinning shape and not property.
findings.suggested_fix: Narrow `CloseAccountResult` so the success statuses carry no `message` (keep it on `{status:'error'}`), drop the two `ACCOUNT_CLOSE_COPY` lookups from `closeAccountAction`, and reword its JSDoc so it describes what the function does — POST the closure, map FAMILY_DELETION_REQUIRED and the step-up — and says that what the parent reads is decided by `accountClosedDeviceMessage` from the reported device outcome. Rewrite parent-privacy.test.ts:475-487 to assert the status and the recorded call, and leave the sentence assertions where they already belong, on `accountClosedDeviceMessage`.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: HUNT6-J-7: `cancelScan` has no throwing path, so the `.catch(() => undefined)` removed from `changePages` was dead code and both callers may now treat it as answering rather than throwing.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Enumerated every statement of `cancelScan` (apps/mobile/src/homework/upload.ts:143-160): the only statement outside the try is `if (attempt.assignmentId === null) return 'nothing_to_cancel';`, and the `api.send` call is inside the try, so even a synchronous throw from the client becomes a caught rejection; the catch returns 'unsure' for every error, typed or not. Then checked the consequence at the other caller: the abort path does `stoppedScanOutcome(await cancelScan(...))` inside `send()`'s own catch (scan.tsx:286), where a rejection would escape a `void send()` as an unhandled rejection. Grepped the mobile tree for other callers.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: Only two callers exist (scan.tsx:131 and scan.tsx:286) and neither can observe a rejection, because none is producible. The removal of the handler is correct and the surviving asymmetry with the abort path is genuinely deliberate.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: HUNT6-J-4: keeping the attempt on 'nothing_to_cancel' is safe because "a retained createKey can only ever address the same pages, because any change to them mints a fresh attempt", and "the create route answers a key it has seen with the assignment it already has".
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Grepped every mutation of the scan session in apps/mobile/app/(child)/scan.tsx (`setSession` at 134 and 305 only; `changePages` at 162, 244, 457, 463, 474) to find a page change that does not rotate the attempt, and tried to construct a sequence where a retained createKey meets a different page set. Then read POST /v1/assignments (apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:703-779) to check the idempotency lookup, and traced whether a finalize could ever have committed while `assignmentId` is still null (it cannot: `base` is built from the create response, and `onAttempt` always fires with it, upload.ts:71-73).
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: Every page change goes through `changePages` or `startOver`, both of which call `newAttempt(newKey)`, so a retained key can only re-address the same pages; and the route resolves a seen `family:key` to the existing row before any insert, so the retry yields one assignment, not two. The only crack I found is narrow and pre-existing: `existing()` throws CONFLICT for a row whose status became 'deleted' (homework.ts:743-745), which a retained key would then hit forever with generic copy — unreachable inside one screen session, and it predates this change, so I did not file it.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: One job, one charge survives a cancel being issued more than once for the same assignment (the abort path can answer 'unsure' after the request actually landed, and `changePages` can then cancel the same id again).
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Read POST /v1/assignments/:id/cancel (apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:1040-1090) looking for a second allowance release or a second job cancellation on a repeat call, and traced the sequence 'unsure' → attempt kept with its assignmentId → child edits a page → `changePages` cancels the same id.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: A cancel of an already-'cancelled' assignment returns early before any write (homework.ts:1061-1063), and the release is scoped to `usage_reservations … where status = 'reserved'`, so a repeat is a no-op. No double release, no double charge, no double job cancellation.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: `sessionEndConfirmed: true` really means the parent session is gone from this device (the fact HUNT6-J-1 exists to make observable).
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Looked for a swallowed failure between `parentAuth.signOut()` answering ok and the keychain actually losing the session: read auth-js 2.116 `_signOut` and `_removeSession`, then apps/mobile/src/lib/chunked-storage.ts `removeItem` (the storage adapter the client is constructed with, parent-auth.ts:35) for a `.catch` on any `store.deleteItem`, and checked `signOutParent`'s consumption of `.ok` (apps/mobile/src/lib/mode.ts:322-325) for a re-swallow.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: `_signOut` returns `{error: null}` only after `removeCurrentSession()`; `_removeSession` awaits `removeItemAsync` unguarded; `chunked-storage.removeItem` deletes the pointer first and propagates every rejection; and `signOutParent` maps a rejection to `false` rather than hiding it. A keychain removal that fails therefore reaches the parent as an unconfirmed sign-out. (Its sibling flag `secretsCleared` does not hold — filed as HUNT7-K-1.)

properties_attacked_and_held.property: Every upload limit the mobile client enforces also exists on the server, so no limit is client-only.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Enumerated each check in `uploadScan` (apps/mobile/src/homework/upload.ts:177-198) — allowed MIME type, declared pixel size, per-page bytes, total scan bytes — plus page count, and searched for each one's server counterpart.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: Page count: `body.pageCount > config.limits.maxPages` → TOO_MANY_PAGES (apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:713-718). Type and per-page bytes: `validatePages(pages, config, caller)` at registration (homework.ts:786). Total bytes: the same `homeworkScanFits` constant at registration (homework.ts:646-650) and again in the scan job (apps/api/src/jobs/scan-process.ts:1363-1366). Pixel size: HOMEWORK_IMAGE_LIMITS is re-checked from the real image header server-side (apps/api/src/services/image-metadata.ts:24). Each client refusal has a matching server rule with child-safe copy in RULE_COPY.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: The closure outcome the parent is meant to read survives the sign-out that ends their session, on the mobile privacy screen.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Looked for a re-gate that would replace the 'account_closed' section: `useParentAccess` renders `<ParentAccessState>` instead of the body whenever `access.status !== 'ready'` (apps/mobile/app/(parent)/privacy.tsx:255-268), so I checked whether it re-checks on an auth change, on focus, or on app state, and whether pull-to-refresh or the reload effect could overwrite the outcome.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: `useParentAccess` deliberately does not subscribe to `parentAuth.watch` (apps/mobile/src/family/ui.tsx:344-353 states that reason explicitly), only to focus and foreground; and `closureStarted` is a ref checked inside `load` itself (privacy.tsx:117) as well as on the reload effect, so the pull-to-refresh door found in round 6 is closed. The outcome stays on screen until the parent taps Done.

properties_attacked_and_held.property: `loadPrivacyOverview` still works for a parent whose family has been deleted — the state in which they most need the deletion rows.
properties_attacked_and_held.how_you_attacked_it: Noticed that three of the four parallel calls swallow NOT_FOUND and `/v1/deletion` does not (apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.ts:364-378), then read GET /v1/deletion (apps/api/src/routes/privacy.ts:712-734) to see whether a family-less or tombstoned-family caller can get a 404 and so blank the whole screen with an error.
properties_attacked_and_held.why_it_held: That route is scoped to `requested_by = caller` plus the open requests of a tombstoned family, reads with the service role precisely because the family is invisible to RLS, and needs no live family — so it answers 200 with rows and the missing `.catch` cannot fire.
